  <Tab value="Go">
    ```go
    package main
    import ("bytes"; "encoding/base64"; "encoding/json"; "fmt"; "io"; "net/http"; "os"; "time"; "strings")
    func check(err error) { if err != nil { panic(err) } }
    func main() {
     key:=os.Getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"); if key=="" { panic("请设置 GEMINI_API_KEY") }
     base:=os.Getenv("GEMINI_BASE_URL"); if base=="" {base="https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com"}
     req,err:=http.NewRequest("POST", strings.TrimRight(base,"/")+"/v1beta/interactions", bytes.NewBufferString(`{"model":"gemini-3.8-flash-tts","input":[{"type":"user_input","content":[{"type":"text","text":"祝你今天过得愉快。","annotations":[{"type":"speech_metadata","style":"温暖自然"}]}]}],"response_format":{"type":"audio"},"generation_config":{"speech_config":[{"voice":"Kore"}]}}`));check(err)
     req.Header.Set("x-goog-api-key",key);req.Header.Set("Content-Type","application/json")
     res,err:=(&http.Client{Timeout:180*time.Second}).Do(req);check(err);defer res.Body.Close()
     raw,err:=io.ReadAll(res.Body);check(err);if res.StatusCode>=300 {panic(fmt.Sprintf("HTTP %d: %s",res.StatusCode,raw))}
     var result struct {Status string `json:"status"`; Steps []struct {Type string `json:"type"`;Content []struct {Type string `json:"type"`;Mime string `json:"mime_type"`;Data string `json:"data"`} `json:"content"`} `json:"steps"`}
     check(json.Unmarshal(raw,&result));if result.Status!="completed" {panic("生成未完成")}
     count:=0
     for _,step:=range result.Steps { if step.Type!="model_output" {continue}; for _,part:=range step.Content {if part.Type!="audio" {continue}
     if part.Mime!="audio/wav" && part.Mime!="audio/x-wav" && part.Mime!="audio/wave" {panic("响应不是 WAV")}
     data,err:=base64.StdEncoding.Strict().DecodeString(part.Data);check(err);if len(data)==0 {panic("音频为空")}
     count++;name:=fmt.Sprintf("speech-%d.wav",count);out,err:=os.OpenFile(name,os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL,0600);check(err)
     _,err=out.Write(data);closeErr:=out.Close();check(err);check(closeErr);fmt.Println(name)
     }};if count==0 {panic("响应没有音频")}
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Errors

| HTTP status           | Meaning and action                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 400                   | Invalid request fields or model parameters; correct the request before resubmitting.                                                 |
| 401                   | Missing, invalid, or expired API key.                                                                                                |
| 403                   | No access to the project or model.                                                                                                   |
| 404                   | Model or route not found; check the address and model ID.                                                                            |
| 429                   | Rate or quota limit; distinguish insufficient funds from retryable throttling.                                                       |
| 500 / 502 / 503 / 504 | Service or upstream failure. Keep the request ID and back off for temporary faults; do not retry the same paid request indefinitely. |

Google error objects use `error.code`, `error.status`, and `error.message`; never infer the source from the HTTP number alone. This endpoint is synchronous\: there is no task ID or polling stage. Never decode error text as audio data.

## Official reference

[Google Gemini TTS](https\://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/speech-generation), [Interactions](https\://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/interactions).

# Audio

Audio APIs convert text to speech, recordings to text, and analyze audio. Speech, music generation, and video soundtracks are different capabilities; do not mix models or endpoints.

## Overview

| What you want to do                            | Direction                  | Typical output                              | Billing unit                            |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Read text aloud, produce voice-over            | Text → speech              | Audio files such as MP3 and WAV             | Input characters or audio duration      |
| Turn a recording into text                     | Speech → text              | Original-language text, timestamps          | Seconds or minutes of audio             |
| Turn a foreign-language recording into English | Speech → English text      | English text, without the original language | Audio duration                          |
| Understand recording content                   | Speech → analysis text     | Summary, speakers, conclusions              | Tokens corresponding to the input audio |
| Hold a realtime conversation                   | Bidirectional audio stream | Continuous audio and events                 | Session duration or Tokens              |

## Core concepts

* **Sample rate**\: samples per second, commonly 16kHz (sufficient for speech recognition) and 24kHz or 44.1kHz (higher fidelity). A mismatched sample rate causes pitch shifts on playback or lower transcription quality.
* **Bit depth and channels**\: 16 bit mono is the common choice for speech; stereo and higher bit depths increase file size without the model necessarily using them.
* **Container and codec**\: MP3 is lossy and small; WAV is usually uncompressed and large; PCM is raw samples without a container, so playback needs the sampling specification supplied manually.
* **Duration and size**\: upload limits often constrain file size and duration together. Converting to a higher sample rate does not improve recognition accuracy, only makes limits easier to hit.
* **Synchronous vs. streaming**\: TTS returns audio bytes and ASR returns JSON. Streaming reduces time to the first word or first segment without changing the total billed amount.

Specification values (maximum duration, supported formats, sample-rate ranges) depend on the model; see each endpoint page's request parameter table.

## Endpoint overview

| Capability                 | Input → output                                  | Request mode                                                    | Documentation                                 |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Speech synthesis (TTS)     | Text → audio                                    | One HTTP request; some models support chunked audio or SSE      | [Text to speech](/simidoc/en/apps/api/audio/speech)                    |
| Speech recognition (ASR)   | Audio file → original-language text             | Multipart upload; some models support transcription SSE         | [Audio transcription](/simidoc/en/apps/api/audio/transcriptions)       |
| Speech translation         | Multilingual audio → English text               | One multipart request                                           | [Audio translation](/simidoc/en/apps/api/audio/translations)           |
| Gemini speech synthesis    | Text → single- or multi-speaker audio           | Native Interactions; supported older models use generateContent | [Gemini TTS](/simidoc/en/apps/api/audio/gemini)                        |
| Gemini audio understanding | Recording → summary, transcript, or analysis    | Native multimodal request                                       | [Audio understanding](/simidoc/en/apps/api/audio/gemini-understanding) |
| MiMo speech                | Text/reference voice → speech; recording → text | Independent compatibility routes or official Chat Completions   | [MiMo](/simidoc/en/apps/api/audio/mimo-audio)                          |
| Realtime speech            | Continuous input and output                     | WebRTC / bidirectional WebSocket                                | [Realtime](/simidoc/en/apps/api/pending/realtime)               |

## Synchronous, asynchronous, and streaming modes

* **Synchronous HTTP**\: one request returns audio or a complete transcript, without a task ID or polling.
* **HTTP streaming**\: one response delivers audio chunks or SSE events. It is not a bidirectional realtime session; do not JSON-parse binary audio.
* **Asynchronous task**\: receive an ID, then query status. Video generation commonly uses this flow; ordinary TTS/ASR does not.
* **Realtime**\: keep a session connected to send audio continuously, interrupt playback, and handle events. File upload is not a substitute.

## Simulated call

A speech synthesis request body is JSON, yet the response is audio bytes rather than JSON\:

```json
{
  "model": "gpt-4o-mini-tts",
  "voice": "alloy",
  "input": "欢迎使用 SimiRouter。",
  "response_format": "mp3"
}
```

The response headers decide how to save the file; write the body straight to `.mp3`\:

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: audio/mpeg
Content-Length: 24576

<二进制音频数据>
```

Transcription uploads multipart and returns JSON\:

```json
{"text":"欢迎使用 SimiRouter。"}
```

Within the same audio category, synthesis returns binary and transcription returns JSON, so the parsers cannot be mixed. The example model `gpt-4o-mini-tts` is marked deprecated by the vendor; see [Text to speech](/simidoc/en/apps/api/audio/speech) for the replacement and migration path.

## Prerequisites

OpenAI-compatible pages use SimiRouter addresses and keys; native references use vendor addresses and keys. Account model lists and channel permissions determine availability. Do not assume every vendor capability is proxied. Obtain recording consent; voice cloning requires usage rights and disclosure of synthetic speech.

## Official references

* [OpenAI speech synthesis](https\://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/audio/subresources/speech/methods/create)
* [OpenAI audio transcription](https\://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/audio/subresources/transcriptions/methods/create)
* [OpenAI audio translation](https\://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/audio/subresources/translations/methods/create)
* [Google audio understanding](https\://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/audio)
* [Google Gemini TTS](https\://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/speech-generation)

# MiMo audio integration

## Endpoint overview

MiMo supports speech synthesis, transcription, voice design, and reference-voice cloning. Distinguish these interfaces\:

| Protocol                             | Address / endpoint                                                     | Authentication                                           | Output                               |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Independent compatible audio service | Deployment address plus `/v1/audio/speech`, `/v1/audio/transcriptions` | The service’s own Bearer key; x-api-key is also accepted | Audio bytes or transcription results |
| Xiaomi native API                    | `https://api.xiaomimimo.com/v1/chat/completions`                       | Official MiMo api-key or Bearer key                      | Chat Completions JSON / SSE          |

**The compatibility route is not Xiaomi’s native endpoint.** Compatible examples default to the independent service at `http://127.0.0.1:8080`. Replace host and port for other deployments. Confirm equivalent SimiRouter routing separately; its key is not interchangeable with the service key.

## Request parameters

### Speech synthesis\: POST /v1/audio/speech

| Field            | Type            | Required | Description                                                                                                  |
| ---------------- | --------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| model            | string          | Yes      | mimo-v2.5-tts, mimo-v2.5-tts-voicedesign, mimo-v2.5-tts-voiceclone.                                          |
| input            | string          | Yes      | Nonempty text; default maximum 4096 characters, configurable by deployment.                                  |
| voice            | string / object | Yes      | Preset voice; for cloning, an audio data URL or service-created \{"id"\:"voice\_..."}.                       |
| instructions     | string          | No       | Tone/style instructions, up to 4096 characters.                                                              |
| style            | string          | No       | Compatibility extension taking precedence over instructions; voicedesign uses it to describe the voice.      |
| speed            | number          | No       | 0.25–4, default 1; converted to a style prompt, not guaranteed sample-accurate speed control.                |
| response\_format | string          | No       | wav, mp3, opus, aac, flac, pcm. Direct MiMo defaults to wav; specify explicitly.                             |
| stream\_format   | string          | No       | The service accepts audio only; sse returns 400. It does not expose a low-latency upstream synthesis stream. |

Preset mapping\: alloy→Bingtang, echo→Moli, fable→Baihua, onyx→Suda, nova→Mia, shimmer→Chloe, dean→Dean, milo→Milo. These service mappings are not OpenAI’s same-named voices.

### Transcription\: POST /v1/audio/transcriptions

| Field                       | Type      | Required | Description                                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | --------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| file                        | file      | Yes      | Multipart file; default maximum 25 MiB, configurable by deployment.                                    |
| model                       | string    | Yes      | mimo-v2.5-asr.                                                                                         |
| language                    | string    | No       | auto (default), zh, en.                                                                                |
| languages\[]                | string\[] | No       | Candidate languages, mutually exclusive with language; multiple candidates become automatic detection. |
| response\_format            | string    | No       | json (default), text, verbose\_json, srt, vtt. diarized\_json is unsupported.                          |
| stream                      | boolean   | No       | SSE is emitted after transcription completes, not while the upstream listens.                          |
| timestamp\_granularities\[] | string\[] | No       | Unsupported; a nonempty value returns 400. Word or segment timestamps are not fabricated.              |

The service accepts mp3, wav, aac, flac, m4a, mp4, mpeg, mpga, oga, ogg, opus, and webm; non-native formats need media conversion. Xiaomi native ASR accepts only MP3/WAV; do not interchange these limits.

## Response

* Successful TTS returns audio bytes with the appropriate MIME type after synthesis completes; no public task\_id is provided.
* ASR JSON is `{"text":"识别文字"}`; text returns plain text directly.
* verbose\_json contains task, language, duration, text, and empty segments, but **does not provide real segment timestamps**. SRT/VTT covers the whole recording, not word alignment.
* stream=true wraps the final transcript in SSE; it does not prove realtime upstream recognition.

## Code examples

Python examples require `python3 -m pip install requests`; Node.js uses version 18+ with built-in fetch; Go uses standard libraries.

### Text to speech

Set the independent service’s `MIMO_AUDIO_API_KEY`. Output is `mimo-speech.wav`.

<Tabs items={["Python","Node.js","curl","Go"]}>
  <Tab value="Python">
    ```python
    import os
    import requests
    from pathlib import Path

    url = 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/audio/speech'
    headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + os.environ['MIMO_AUDIO_API_KEY']}
    response = requests.request('POST', url, headers=headers, json={'model': 'mimo-v2.5-tts', 'input': '你好，欢迎使用 MiMo 语音。', 'voice': 'alloy', 'response_format': 'wav'}, timeout=180)
    response.raise_for_status()
    Path('mimo-speech.wav').write_bytes(response.content)
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="Node.js">
    ```javascript
    async function main() {
      const url = "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/audio/speech";
      const headers = { "Authorization": "Bearer " + process.env.MIMO_AUDIO_API_KEY };
      headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json";
      const body = JSON.stringify({
      "model": "mimo-v2.5-tts",
      "input": "你好，欢迎使用 MiMo 语音。",
      "voice": "alloy",
      "response_format": "wav"
    });
      const response = await fetch(url, { method: "POST", headers, body, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(180000) });
      if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}: ${await response.text()}`);
      const { writeFile } = require("node:fs/promises");
      await writeFile("mimo-speech.wav", Buffer.from(await response.arrayBuffer()));
    }
    main().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode = 1; });
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="curl">
    ```bash
    set -eu
    [ ! -e "mimo-speech.wav" ] || { printf '%s\n' "目标文件已存在：mimo-speech.wav" >&2; exit 1; }
    temporary=$(mktemp)
    trap 'rm -f "$temporary"' EXIT
    if curl --fail-with-body --max-time 180 -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/audio/speech" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $MIMO_AUDIO_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      --data-binary '{
      "model": "mimo-v2.5-tts",
      "input": "你好，欢迎使用 MiMo 语音。",
      "voice": "alloy",
      "response_format": "wav"
    }' \
      --output "$temporary"; then
      mv "$temporary" "mimo-speech.wav"
    else
      status=$?
      cat "$temporary" >&2
      exit "$status"
    fi
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="Go">
    ```go
    package main

    import (
      "fmt"
      "io"
      "net/http"
      "os"
      "time"
      "strings"
    )

    func check(err error) { if err != nil { panic(err) } }
    func main() {
      body := strings.NewReader(`{
      "model": "mimo-v2.5-tts",
      "input": "你好，欢迎使用 MiMo 语音。",
      "voice": "alloy",
      "response_format": "wav"
    }`)
      req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/audio/speech", body); check(err)
      req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer " + os.Getenv("MIMO_AUDIO_API_KEY"))
      req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
      client := &http.Client{Timeout: 180 * time.Second}
      res, err := client.Do(req); check(err)
      defer res.Body.Close()
      data, err := io.ReadAll(res.Body); check(err)
      if res.StatusCode < 200 || res.StatusCode >= 300 { panic(fmt.Sprintf("HTTP %d: %s", res.StatusCode, data)) }
      check(os.WriteFile("mimo-speech.wav", data, 0600))
    }
    ```

</Tabs>

### Speech to text

Prepare `speech.wav`. Authentication still uses the independent service key.

<Tabs items={["Python","Node.js","curl","Go"]}>
  <Tab value="Python">
    ```python
    import os
    import requests

    url = 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/audio/transcriptions'
    headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + os.environ['MIMO_AUDIO_API_KEY']}
    with open('speech.wav', "rb") as source:
        response = requests.request('POST', url, headers=headers, data={'model': 'mimo-v2.5-asr', 'language': 'auto', 'response_format': 'json'}, files={'file': source}, timeout=180)
    response.raise_for_status()
    print(response.text)
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="Node.js">
    ```javascript
    async function main() {
      const url = "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/audio/transcriptions";
      const headers = { "Authorization": "Bearer " + process.env.MIMO_AUDIO_API_KEY };
      const { readFile } = require("node:fs/promises");
      const form = new FormData();
      form.append("file", new Blob([await readFile("speech.wav")]), "speech.wav");
      form.append("model", "mimo-v2.5-asr");
      form.append("language", "auto");
      form.append("response_format", "json");
      const body = form;
      const response = await fetch(url, { method: "POST", headers, body, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(180000) });
      if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}: ${await response.text()}`);
      console.log(await response.text());
    }
    main().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode = 1; });
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="curl">
    ```bash
    curl "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/audio/transcriptions" \
      --fail-with-body \
      --max-time 180 \
      -X POST \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $MIMO_AUDIO_API_KEY" \
      -F "file=@speech.wav" \
      -F "model=mimo-v2.5-asr" \
      -F "language=auto" \
      -F "response_format=json"
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="Go">
    ```go
    package main

    import (
      "fmt"
      "io"
      "net/http"
      "os"
      "time"
      "bytes"
      "mime/multipart"
    )

    func check(err error) { if err != nil { panic(err) } }
    func main() {
      var buffer bytes.Buffer
      writer := multipart.NewWriter(&buffer)
      source, err := os.Open("speech.wav"); check(err)
      part, err := writer.CreateFormFile("file", "speech.wav"); check(err)
      _, err = io.Copy(part, source); source.Close(); check(err)
      check(writer.WriteField("model", "mimo-v2.5-asr"))
      check(writer.WriteField("language", "auto"))
      check(writer.WriteField("response_format", "json"))
      check(writer.Close())
      req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/audio/transcriptions", &buffer); check(err)
      req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer " + os.Getenv("MIMO_AUDIO_API_KEY"))
      req.Header.Set("Content-Type", writer.FormDataContentType())
      client := &http.Client{Timeout: 180 * time.Second}
      res, err := client.Do(req); check(err)
      defer res.Body.Close()
      data, err := io.ReadAll(res.Body); check(err)
      if res.StatusCode < 200 || res.StatusCode >= 300 { panic(fmt.Sprintf("HTTP %d: %s", res.StatusCode, data)) }
      fmt.Println(string(data))
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

### Voice design and cloning

For voice design, change model to `mimo-v2.5-tts-voicedesign` and add `style: "温暖低沉的成年男声，普通话清晰"`. For cloning, change model to `mimo-v2.5-tts-voiceclone` and set voice to `data:audio/wav;base64,<真实参考音频>`. Never send empty Base64, disguise a file extension, or clone another person without authorization.

```python
import base64
import os
from pathlib import Path
import requests
reference = base64.b64encode(Path("reference.wav").read_bytes()).decode("ascii")
response = requests.post("http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/audio/speech",
    headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["MIMO_AUDIO_API_KEY"]},
    json={"model":"mimo-v2.5-tts-voiceclone","input":"这是一条授权声音示例。",
          "voice":"data:audio/wav;base64," + reference,"response_format":"wav"}, timeout=180)
response.raise_for_status()
Path("clone.wav").write_bytes(response.content)
```

### Xiaomi native protocol

Official TTS puts spoken text in an `assistant` message and style instructions in a `user` message. This is official JSON, not a request for `/audio/speech`\:

```json
{"model":"mimo-v2.5-tts","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"温暖自然"},{"role":"assistant","content":"你好，欢迎使用 MiMo。"}],"audio":{"format":"wav","voice":"mimo_default"},"stream":false}
```

Official returned audio is in `choices[0].message.audio.data` and needs Base64 decoding. Native ASR places audio in `messages[0].content`\:

```json
{"model":"mimo-v2.5-asr","messages":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_audio","input_audio":{"data":"data:audio/wav;base64,<真实Base64>"}}]}],"asr_options":{"language":"auto"},"stream":false}
```

Native ASR text is in `choices[0].message.content`. format is optional for a typed data URL; bare Base64 requires `format: "wav"` or `"mp3"`. If both are supplied, they must agree.

## Errors

| HTTP / code                       | Meaning                                               |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| 400 / unsupported\_audio\_format  | Invalid TTS output format.                            |
| 400 / speech\_sse\_not\_supported | The compatibility service does not support TTS SSE.   |
| 400 / diarization\_not\_supported | ASR does not support speaker diarization output.      |
| 400 / timestamps\_not\_supported  | ASR does not support timestamp granularity.           |
| 401 / 403                         | Invalid independent service key or permissions.       |
| 404 / voice\_not\_found           | Custom voice missing or not owned by the current key. |
| 413 / input\_too\_large           | Text or media exceeds limits.                         |
| 415 / unsupported\_file\_type     | Unsupported extension or MIME type.                   |
| 422 / invalid\_audio              | Media cannot be decoded.                              |
| 502 / invalid\_audio\_output      | Upstream returned no valid audio.                     |
| 503 / audio\_failover\_exhausted  | Audio service temporarily unavailable.                |

Uploading a cloned voice changes service state. Do not blindly repeat after a timeout.

## Official reference

[MiMo TTS](https\://mimo.mi.com/docs/en-US/api/audio/tts), [MiMo ASR](https\://mimo.mi.com/docs/en-US/api/audio/Speech-Recognition). These official pages describe native protocols, not compatibility extensions as vendor capabilities.

# OpenAI audio format

## Endpoint overview

The OpenAI audio format has three separate HTTP endpoints, all using `Authorization: Bearer $SIMIROUTER_API_KEY`.

| Endpoint                        | Content type        | Response                                     | Documentation                            |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `POST /v1/audio/speech`         | JSON                | Audio bytes; SSE when supported by the model | [Speech synthesis](/simidoc/en/apps/api/audio/speech)             |
| `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` | multipart/form-data | Transcription JSON, text, or subtitles       | [Speech transcription](/simidoc/en/apps/api/audio/transcriptions) |
| `POST /v1/audio/translations`   | multipart/form-data | English translation text or subtitles        | [Speech translation](/simidoc/en/apps/api/audio/translations)     |

Request `model` must be an audio model available to the account. TTS `voice`, transcription output formats, timestamps, and streaming capabilities vary by model and are not interchangeable. File transcription does not provide a continuous microphone session; see [Realtime](/simidoc/en/apps/api/pending/realtime).

This page references the OpenAI API format. Model lifecycle and vendor parameters follow each endpoint’s official API Reference. Gateway keys and official OpenAI keys are not interchangeable.

# Text to speech

## Endpoint overview

`POST /v1/audio/speech` synthesizes `input` into speech. For SimiRouter, the base URL is `https://api.dwchainless.com` with authentication `Authorization: Bearer $SIMIROUTER_API_KEY` and the body is `application/json`. This page references the official OpenAI Speech API; model availability and parameter passthrough depend on the selected channel.

<Callout type="warn" title="Models shut down on 2027-01-06">
  `gpt-4o-mini-tts`, `tts-1`, and `tts-1-hd` are deprecated by OpenAI and shut down on 2027-01-06. The official replacement is `gpt-realtime-2.1-mini` on the Realtime API, which does not support `/v1/audio/speech`; migrate through `/v1/realtime`. Examples still use a currently routable model; confirm the channel offers a replacement before calling.
</Callout>

## Request parameters

| Field            | Type            | Required | Description                                                                                   |
| ---------------- | --------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| model            | string          | Yes      | An available TTS model, such as gpt-4o-mini-tts; transcription models are not supported here. |
| input            | string          | Yes      | Text to read, up to 4,096 characters.                                                         |
| voice            | string / object | Yes      | A built-in voice name or an authorized custom voice \{"id"\:"voice\_..."}.                    |
| instructions     | string          | No       | Tone and style instructions; not supported by tts-1/tts-1-hd. Up to 4,096 characters.         |
| response\_format | string          | No       | mp3 (default), opus, aac, flac, wav, or pcm.                                                  |
| speed            | number          | No       | 0.25–4.0; default 1.                                                                          |
| stream\_format   | string          | No       | audio (default) or sse; tts-1/tts-1-hd do not support sse.                                    |

Built-in voices include `alloy`, `ash`, `ballad`, `coral`, `echo`, `fable`, `onyx`, `nova`, `sage`, `shimmer`, `verse`, `marin`, `cedar`; a model may support only a subset. Voice names do not designate a fixed language.

## Response

A successful response contains audio bytes, not JSON with a URL. Match the saved file extension to `response_format`. PCM contains raw samples without a container and requires the correct playback settings. The default audio response can be read incrementally to reduce latency.

`stream_format: "sse"` uses an event stream. Parse events and decode audio deltas; do not save the full SSE text as MP3. SSE availability also depends on the channel implementation.

## Code examples

Python examples require `python3 -m pip install requests`; Node.js uses version 18+ with built-in fetch; Go uses standard libraries.

First set `SIMIROUTER_API_KEY`. The examples select MP3 and stop on HTTP errors to avoid writing an error JSON response as audio.

<Tabs items={["Python","Node.js","curl","Go"]}>
  <Tab value="Python">
    ```python
    import os
    import requests
    from pathlib import Path

    url = 'https://api.dwchainless.com/v1/audio/speech'
    headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + os.environ['SIMIROUTER_API_KEY']}
    response = requests.request('POST', url, headers=headers, json={'model': 'gpt-4o-mini-tts', 'input': '你好，欢迎使用语音合成。', 'voice': 'alloy', 'response_format': 'mp3'}, timeout=180)
    response.raise_for_status()
    Path('speech.mp3').write_bytes(response.content)
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="Node.js">
    ```javascript
    async function main() {
      const url = "https://api.dwchainless.com/v1/audio/speech";
      const headers = { "Authorization": "Bearer " + process.env.SIMIROUTER_API_KEY };
      headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json";
      const body = JSON.stringify({
      "model": "gpt-4o-mini-tts",
      "input": "你好，欢迎使用语音合成。",
      "voice": "alloy",
      "response_format": "mp3"
    });
      const response = await fetch(url, { method: "POST", headers, body, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(180000) });
      if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}: ${await response.text()}`);
      const { writeFile } = require("node:fs/promises");
      await writeFile("speech.mp3", Buffer.from(await response.arrayBuffer()));
    }
    main().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode = 1; });
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="curl">
    ```bash
    set -eu
    [ ! -e "speech.mp3" ] || { printf '%s\n' "目标文件已存在：speech.mp3" >&2; exit 1; }
    temporary=$(mktemp)
    trap 'rm -f "$temporary"' EXIT
    if curl --fail-with-body --max-time 180 -X POST "https://api.dwchainless.com/v1/audio/speech" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $SIMIROUTER_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      --data-binary '{
      "model": "gpt-4o-mini-tts",
      "input": "你好，欢迎使用语音合成。",
      "voice": "alloy",
      "response_format": "mp3"
    }' \
      --output "$temporary"; then
      mv "$temporary" "speech.mp3"
    else
      status=$?
      cat "$temporary" >&2
      exit "$status"
    fi
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="Go">
    ```go
    package main

    import (
      "fmt"
      "io"
      "net/http"
      "os"
      "time"
      "strings"
    )

    func check(err error) { if err != nil { panic(err) } }
    func main() {
      body := strings.NewReader(`{
      "model": "gpt-4o-mini-tts",
      "input": "你好，欢迎使用语音合成。",
      "voice": "alloy",
      "response_format": "mp3"
    }`)
      req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.dwchainless.com/v1/audio/speech", body); check(err)
      req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer " + os.Getenv("SIMIROUTER_API_KEY"))
      req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
      client := &http.Client{Timeout: 180 * time.Second}
      res, err := client.Do(req); check(err)
      defer res.Body.Close()
      data, err := io.ReadAll(res.Body); check(err)
      if res.StatusCode < 200 || res.StatusCode >= 300 { panic(fmt.Sprintf("HTTP %d: %s", res.StatusCode, data)) }
      check(os.WriteFile("speech.mp3", data, 0600))
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Errors

| HTTP status           | Meaning and action                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 400                   | Invalid request fields or model parameters; correct the request before resubmitting.                                                 |
| 401                   | Missing, invalid, or expired API key.                                                                                                |
| 403                   | No access to the project or model.                                                                                                   |
| 404                   | Model or route not found; check the address and model ID.                                                                            |
| 429                   | Rate or quota limit; distinguish insufficient funds from retryable throttling.                                                       |
| 500 / 502 / 503 / 504 | Service or upstream failure. Keep the request ID and back off for temporary faults; do not retry the same paid request indefinitely. |

The error body’s `error.message`, `error.type`, and `error.code` give more specific reasons than the HTTP status. This endpoint is synchronous\: there is no task ID or polling stage. Never save error text as an audio file.

## Official reference

[OpenAI Create speech](https\://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/audio/subresources/speech/methods/create).

# Audio transcription

## Endpoint overview

`POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` with authentication `Authorization: Bearer $SIMIROUTER_API_KEY`. Upload with `multipart/form-data` and let the HTTP library generate the boundary; do not manually set Content-Type without a boundary.

This endpoint preserves the original language and does not automatically translate Chinese into English. Supported file formats include flac, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, ogg, wav, and webm. File size and recording duration are also subject to model and channel limits.

<Callout type="warn" title="Some models shut down on 2027-02-26">
  `whisper-1`, `gpt-4o-transcribe`, and `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` (including dated snapshots) are deprecated and shut down on 2027-02-26. Prefer `gpt-transcribe`; use `gpt-live-transcribe` for live audio or `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize` when you need speaker labels.
</Callout>

## Request parameters

| Field                         | Type            | Required    | Description                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------- | --------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| file                          | file            | Yes         | The audio file itself, not a path string or ordinary URL.                                                  |
| model                         | string          | Yes         | For example, gpt-transcribe, gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, whisper-1, or a diarization model. |
| language                      | string          | No          | The input language’s ISO-639-1 code, such as zh or en.                                                     |
| languages\[]                  | string\[]       | No          | Candidate languages; use only with models that support this field.                                         |
| prompt                        | string          | No          | Terminology and contextual hints in the recording’s language; not supported by diarization models.         |
| keywords\[]                   | string\[]       | No          | Terminology hints; gpt-transcribe only.                                                                    |
| response\_format              | string          | No          | Default json; support for text, srt, vtt, verbose\_json, and diarized\_json varies by model.               |
| temperature                   | number          | No          | 0–1; default 0.                                                                                            |
| stream                        | boolean         | No          | true returns SSE; whisper-1 does not support it.                                                           |
| include\[]                    | string\[]       | No          | logprobs requires a supported model and response\_format=json.                                             |
| timestamp\_granularities\[]   | string\[]       | No          | word / segment; requires verbose\_json and a supported model; not applicable to diarization.               |
| chunking\_strategy            | string / object | Conditional | auto or a server\_vad configuration; required for diarization input over 30 seconds.                       |
| known\_speaker\_names\[]      | string\[]       | No          | Short names for up to four known speakers, paired with audio references.                                   |
| known\_speaker\_references\[] | string\[]       | No          | Audio data URLs lasting 2–10 seconds, paired one-to-one with names, for models that support this feature.  |

`gpt-4o-transcribe` and `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` use JSON output; `whisper-1` supports formats such as text, srt, vtt, and verbose\_json. For speaker labels, use a diarization-capable model and `diarized_json`; do not impose this parameter on ordinary models.

## Response

| Field                    | Description                                                                           |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `text`                   | The complete transcription.                                                           |
| `usage`                  | Model-provided usage statistics; fields vary by model.                                |
| `logprobs`               | Token confidence information when requested and supported.                            |
| `language` / `duration`  | Language and audio duration in seconds for verbose\_json.                             |
| `words[]` / `segments[]` | Segments when timestamps or speaker output is supported; not present in every format. |

```json
{"text":"欢迎参加今天的会议。"}
```

`stream=true` returns transcription deltas and completion events over SSE on supported models. The recipient must keep reading the stream. The complete file is still uploaded first; this is not bidirectional microphone Realtime.

## Code examples

Python examples require `python3 -m pip install requests`; Node.js uses version 18+ with built-in fetch; Go uses standard libraries.

Prepare `speech.wav` and apply `SIMIROUTER_API_KEY`.

<Tabs items={["Python","Node.js","curl","Go"]}>
  <Tab value="Python">
    ```python
    import os
    import requests

    url = 'https://api.dwchainless.com/v1/audio/transcriptions'
    headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + os.environ['SIMIROUTER_API_KEY']}
    with open('speech.wav', "rb") as source:
        response = requests.request('POST', url, headers=headers, data={'model': 'gpt-4o-mini-transcribe', 'response_format': 'json'}, files={'file': source}, timeout=180)
    response.raise_for_status()
    print(response.text)
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="Node.js">
    ```javascript
    async function main() {
      const url = "https://api.dwchainless.com/v1/audio/transcriptions";
      const headers = { "Authorization": "Bearer " + process.env.SIMIROUTER_API_KEY };
      const { readFile } = require("node:fs/promises");
      const form = new FormData();
      form.append("file", new Blob([await readFile("speech.wav")]), "speech.wav");
      form.append("model", "gpt-4o-mini-transcribe");
      form.append("response_format", "json");
      const body = form;
      const response = await fetch(url, { method: "POST", headers, body, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(180000) });
      if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}: ${await response.text()}`);
      console.log(await response.text());
    }
    main().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode = 1; });
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="curl">
    ```bash
    curl "https://api.dwchainless.com/v1/audio/transcriptions" \
      --fail-with-body \
      --max-time 180 \
      -X POST \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $SIMIROUTER_API_KEY" \
      -F "file=@speech.wav" \
      -F "model=gpt-4o-mini-transcribe" \
      -F "response_format=json"
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="Go">
    ```go
    package main

    import (
      "fmt"
      "io"
      "net/http"
      "os"
      "time"
      "bytes"
      "mime/multipart"
    )

    func check(err error) { if err != nil { panic(err) } }
    func main() {
      var buffer bytes.Buffer
      writer := multipart.NewWriter(&buffer)
      source, err := os.Open("speech.wav"); check(err)
      part, err := writer.CreateFormFile("file", "speech.wav"); check(err)
      _, err = io.Copy(part, source); source.Close(); check(err)
      check(writer.WriteField("model", "gpt-4o-mini-transcribe"))
      check(writer.WriteField("response_format", "json"))
      check(writer.Close())
      req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.dwchainless.com/v1/audio/transcriptions", &buffer); check(err)
      req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer " + os.Getenv("SIMIROUTER_API_KEY"))
      req.Header.Set("Content-Type", writer.FormDataContentType())
      client := &http.Client{Timeout: 180 * time.Second}
      res, err := client.Do(req); check(err)
      defer res.Body.Close()
      data, err := io.ReadAll(res.Body); check(err)
      if res.StatusCode < 200 || res.StatusCode >= 300 { panic(fmt.Sprintf("HTTP %d: %s", res.StatusCode, data)) }
      fmt.Println(string(data))
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Errors

| HTTP status           | Meaning and action                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 400                   | Invalid request fields or model parameters; correct the request before resubmitting.                                                 |
| 401                   | Missing, invalid, or expired API key.                                                                                                |
| 403                   | No access to the project or model.                                                                                                   |
| 404                   | Model or route not found; check the address and model ID.                                                                            |
| 413                   | File exceeds the upload limit; compress it or send a smaller file.                                                                   |
| 429                   | Rate or quota limit; distinguish insufficient funds from retryable throttling.                                                       |
| 500 / 502 / 503 / 504 | Service or upstream failure. Keep the request ID and back off for temporary faults; do not retry the same paid request indefinitely. |

The error body’s `error.message`, `error.type`, and `error.code` give more specific reasons than the HTTP status. This endpoint is synchronous\: there is no task ID or polling stage. Never save error text as a transcript.

# Audio translation

## Endpoint overview

`POST /v1/audio/translations` accepts a recording and outputs **English**; it does not accept an arbitrary target-language parameter. Authentication uses `Authorization: Bearer $SIMIROUTER_API_KEY` and the body is `multipart/form-data`. This page references the official OpenAI Audio Translations API; the account needs a channel for the corresponding model.

<Callout type="warn" title="Endpoint and model shut down on 2027-02-26">
  OpenAI has deprecated `/v1/audio/translations` and `whisper-1`, which shut down on 2027-02-26. The replacement is the Realtime API at `/v1/realtime/translations` with `gpt-realtime-translate`, which requires a separate integration. This page is retained only as pre-migration reference.
</Callout>

## Request parameters

| Field            | Type   | Required | Description                                                                    |
| ---------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| file             | file   | Yes      | The recording file itself; flac, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, ogg, wav, or webm. |
| model            | string | Yes      | This endpoint uses whisper-1, not an ordinary transcription model.             |
| prompt           | string | No       | English terminology or contextual hints.                                       |
| response\_format | string | No       | json (default), text, srt, verbose\_json, or vtt.                              |
| temperature      | number | No       | 0–1; default 0.                                                                |

## Response

JSON returns `text` containing the English translation. `verbose_json` also includes `duration` (seconds), `language` (english), and `segments[]`. Subtitle formats return subtitle text directly and must not be parsed as JSON. This endpoint processes a single file and has no stream parameter; realtime translation uses a separate session interface.

```json
{"text":"Welcome to today's meeting."}
```

# Agent image calls are now included in protocol documentation

Agent tasks are now distributed across the three protocols. Each includes generation and editing templates, configuration, saving results, and failure handling, replacing a separate tutorial oriented toward OpenAI Images\:

* [Agent calls in OpenAI format](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/openai)\: Images generation, JSON editing, and final-event checks.
* [Agent calls in Gemini native format](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/gemini)\: GenerateContent image Parts, MIME types, and multi-turn context.
* [Agent calls in Qwen native format](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/qwen)\: regional Alibaba Cloud configuration, native synchronous calls, and image URL downloads.

Agents still need local execution and response-inspection capabilities; these documents do not install remote Skills. Real requests may incur charges. Confirm the model, specifications, count, and output location before calling. Do not expose keys, overwrite files, or retry automatically. For interface, effect, and specification comparisons, see the [Image API overview](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images).

# Images

Choose the **API protocol**, decide on the **effect**, and then check the **dimensions, quality, format, and image count**. The protocol defines request and response structures, the model and prompt determine the effect, and specifications define the output requirements. These are separate decisions.

Generation and editing return images; image understanding takes images and returns text or structured results. A text-only model does not gain image-generation capabilities when image parameters are added. Before calling, check the exact model ID, supported interfaces, billing group, and quota under [Models and pricing](https://api.dwchainless.com/en/pricing/). Real requests may incur charges.

## Overview

| What you want to do                   | Input                                    | Output                       | Typical endpoint              |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Generate an image from text           | Prompt                                   | A new image                  | `POST /v1/images/generations` |
| Modify an existing image              | Prompt plus one or more reference images | The edited image             | `POST /v1/images/edits`       |
| Generate images inside a conversation | Chat messages plus the image tool        | Mixed image and text results | `POST /v1/responses`          |
| Have the model describe an image      | Image plus a question                    | Text, not a new image        | `POST /v1/chat/completions`   |

## Core concepts

Three kinds of numbers come first; the parameters and prices below only make sense once they are separated\:

* **Pixel dimensions**\: the real width × height, such as `1024x1024`. It sets the actual resolution of the file, not the file size, and it is not a quality tier.
* **Aspect ratio**\: ratios such as `1:1`, `16:9`, and `9:16` only determine the shape of the frame. One ratio can map to several pixel dimensions; naming a ratio does not specify the output size.
* **Resolution tier**\: tiers such as `1K`, `2K`, and `4K`. Vendor-native tiers are defined by longest edge or product line, while this site's per-image billing tiers are classified by longest edge; the names match but the boundaries may not, so neither can be inferred from the other.

There are also three common misconceptions\: `quality` controls rendering quality, not compression quality; PNG, JPEG, and WebP are file formats, and renaming an extension does not convert one to another; Base64 and URL are delivery methods, not resolutions. See section 4 below, "Image specifications and billing", for the itemized comparison.

## 1. APIs\: choose a protocol

Each of the three protocols has its own request parameters, response fields, and examples. Script calls, agent use, saving results, and failure handling are also explained within each protocol, so you do not need to start with a shared tutorial that only applies to OpenAI.

| Protocol                | API / capability                                          | Request endpoint                                        | Main result                                                  | Documentation                                             |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| OpenAI                  | Text-to-image                                             | `POST /v1/images/generations`                           | `data[].b64_json`; compatible models may also return URLs    | [Generation](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/openai/generations)                        |
| OpenAI                  | Image editing / image-to-image                            | `POST /v1/images/edits`                                 | Edited images                                                | [Editing](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/openai/edits)                                 |
| OpenAI                  | Conversational image generation                           | `POST /v1/responses`, using the `image_generation` tool | Image tool results in `output[]`                             | [Conversational generation](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/openai/chat-format)         |
| OpenAI                  | Image understanding                                       | `POST /v1/chat/completions`, with `image_url` input     | Text analysis, not generated images                          | [Image understanding](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/openai/vision)                    |
| Gemini                  | Text-to-image                                             | `POST /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent`           | `candidates[].content.parts[].inlineData`                    | [Generation](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/gemini/generate)                           |
| Gemini                  | Image editing / multi-turn editing                        | Same endpoint, with mixed text and image input          | Images in the returned content parts                         | [Editing](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/gemini/edits)                                 |
| Gemini                  | Image understanding                                       | Same endpoint, using a model with vision input          | Text analysis                                                | [Media understanding](/simidoc/en/apps/api/chat/gemini-media)               |
| Qwen                    | Text-to-image / image editing                             | `POST /v1/images/generations`, `POST /v1/images/edits`  | `data[].url` or `data[].b64_json`                            | [Generation](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/qwen/generations), [Editing](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/qwen/edits) |
| Jimeng / Volcengine Ark | Text-to-image / reference-image generation                | `POST /api/v3/images/generations`                       | `data[].url` or `data[].b64_json`                            | [Generation](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/jimeng)                                    |
| xAI Grok                | Text-to-image / multiple images                           | `POST /v1/images/generations`                           | `data[].url` or `data[].b64_json`                            | [Generation](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/grok)                                      |
| BFL FLUX                | Text-to-image / reference-image generation (asynchronous) | `POST /v1/flux-pro-1.1` and others                      | Take `polling_url` first, then `result.sample` when complete | [Generation](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/flux)                                      |

**The Qwen section uses the native Qwen request body, called through this site's gateway `/v1/images/generations` and `/v1/images/edits`, and returns the uniform `data[]`.** Do not rewrite the request body into OpenAI's `prompt` field; model IDs must use the names actually provided by this site's channel. Jimeng uses the native Volcengine Ark request body; Grok uses the same paths as OpenAI Images, but its frame parameters are `aspect_ratio` and `resolution`; FLUX does not generate images synchronously and must submit a task and then poll `polling_url`. These three cannot copy each other's fields.

Call modes also vary by protocol\: ordinary OpenAI Images requests wait for complete results, and only supported models offer image event streams; Gemini streams through `streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`; the Qwen and Jimeng examples in this directory use synchronous responses; Grok is synchronous by default and can use `deferred` to become a deferred task; FLUX is always asynchronous polling. None becomes a universal task queue simply by adding an “asynchronous” parameter. See [OpenAI](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/openai), [Gemini](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/gemini), [Qwen](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/qwen), [Jimeng](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/jimeng), [Grok](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/grok), and [FLUX](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/flux) for requests, outputs, and completion checks.

## 2. Effects\: choose by your goal

“Watercolor,” “replace the background,” and “product composition” are usually generation or editing tasks, not separate APIs. The following categories describe tasks, not capabilities guaranteed across all models. Check the relevant protocol and model documentation first.

| Desired effect                                                              | Input and prompt focus                                                                        | Interface choice and limitations                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Create from scratch\: illustrations, covers, posters, photorealistic scenes | Describe the subject, composition, style, lighting, and text to render                        | Use text-to-image; check text and details                                                                                  |
| Reference-image variations\: regenerate using a subject or composition      | Provide a reference and distinguish what to keep from what to change                          | Use image editing / image-to-image; pixel-perfect preservation is not guaranteed                                           |
| Style transfer\: photo to watercolor, line art, and more                    | Provide a reference and target style; state whether to preserve the subject and layout        | Use an editing model that accepts reference images                                                                         |
| Replace backgrounds, add or remove objects, or edit locally                 | Specify the area to change; provide a mask where supported                                    | Use editing; mask support and requirements vary by model                                                                   |
| Combine images\: compose products, people, and scenes                       | Explain each reference image's role, the relationships between subjects, and the final layout | Use an editing model with multi-image input and check input-count limits                                                   |
| Iterate over multiple turns\: continue editing a previous result            | Retain the history or references required by the protocol                                     | Use an interface supporting multi-turn image workflows; saving only text does not guarantee that image context is retained |
| Transparent-background assets                                               | Request a real alpha channel, not a white background or a checkerboard drawn into the image   | Select transparency and a format that preserves it only when the model supports them                                       |
| Image understanding, text extraction, chart questions                       | Supply the image and state the analysis goal                                                  | Use image understanding, which returns text rather than an edited image                                                    |

For capabilities and limitations, see [OpenAI image generation](https\://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-generation), [Gemini image generation and editing](https\://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/image-generation), and [Qwen image editing](https\://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/qwen-image-edit-api). Official examples do not establish that the current gateway channel exposes the same capabilities.

## 3. Calling the API\: four steps to your first image

Whichever protocol you choose, a call follows the same order\: confirm configuration, choose an endpoint, send a minimal request, then read and verify the result. The steps below describe only the general flow; the protocol page defines the exact fields.

### 1. Confirm the request URL, key, and model

* **Request URL**\: This site's gateway is `https://api.dwchainless.com`; the endpoint path varies by protocol and operation.
* **Key**\: Create one under [API key management](https://api.dwchainless.com/keys) and send it as `Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY`; never put it in prompts, source code, screenshots, or Git.
* **Model**\: Copy the complete model ID from [Models and pricing](https://api.dwchainless.com/en/pricing/) and confirm that it supports the target endpoint. Generation, editing, and image understanding may use different models.

### 2. Choose an endpoint and request format

Choose an endpoint from the protocol table above, then confirm the request body format\:

| Operation                       | Endpoint (OpenAI format)      | Request format                   |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Text-to-image                   | `POST /v1/images/generations` | JSON                             |
| Image editing / image-to-image  | `POST /v1/images/edits`       | JSON `images[]` or multipart     |
| Conversational image generation | `POST /v1/responses`          | JSON with the image tool enabled |
| Image understanding             | `POST /v1/chat/completions`   | JSON with an `image_url` item    |

Gemini, Qwen, Jimeng, Grok, and FLUX use their own native request fields; do not copy OpenAI fields directly into them.

### 3. Send a minimal request

For the first call, generate one image without streaming to confirm that authentication, the model, and the parameters are valid. The following uses OpenAI generation as an example\:

```bash
API_URL="https://api.dwchainless.com/v1/images/generations"
API_KEY="PASTE_API_KEY_HERE"
curl "$API_URL" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-image-2",
    "prompt": "一只小机器人在图书馆阅读，水彩插画，不要文字。",
    "n": 1,
    "size": "1024x1024",
    "output_format": "png"
  }'
```

Once the response is normal, increase `n`, adjust the size, or enable streaming as needed. See [generation](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/openai/generations) and [editing](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/openai/edits) for complete multilingual examples.

**Response shape (illustrative)**\: a real response contains a very long Base64 string, so only the beginning is kept here. On success, read `data[]` rather than relying on HTTP 200 alone.

```json
{
  "created": 1763366400,
  "data": [{ "b64_json": "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUg..." }],
  "usage": { "input_tokens": 28, "output_tokens": 4160, "total_tokens": 4188 }
}
```

### 4. Read and verify the result

1. **Check the status**\: Only 2xx means the request succeeded; for 4xx, check parameters and permissions; for 5xx or a timeout, first confirm whether the request executed.
2. **Read the result**\: Take images from `data[]`; GPT Image returns `data[].b64_json`, while compatible models may return `data[].url`; do not assume a first item exists.
3. **Save the image**\: Decode Base64 into binary and choose the extension from the actual MIME type; download URLs promptly and without the API key.
4. **Verify**\: Check that the file opens, then confirm actual pixel dimensions, transparency, and content, and inspect usage logs. HTTP 200, an empty `data[]`, or a streaming preview does not mean the final image has been saved.

## 4. Image specifications and billing

### What each request specification controls

| Specification          | Meaning and examples                                                                   | Common confusion                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pixel dimensions       | Actual width × height, such as `1024x1024` or `1536x1024`                              | Not file size, and not automatically a quality tier                                                                                                      |
| Aspect ratio           | `1:1` square, `16:9` landscape, `9:16` portrait                                        | The same ratio can have multiple resolutions; choosing a ratio alone does not specify exact pixel dimensions                                             |
| Resolution tier        | Some models use native parameters such as `1K`, `2K`, and `4K`                         | Actual dimensions also depend on the model and aspect ratio; provider tiers should not be equated directly with this site's per-image billing boundaries |
| Generation quality     | For example, OpenAI's `quality` selects rendering quality                              | Not `size`, or JPEG/WebP compression quality; other models may not have the same parameter                                                               |
| File format            | PNG, JPEG, WebP, and others, according to the actual returned MIME type                | Base64 and URLs are delivery methods, not image formats; renaming an extension does not convert a file                                                   |
| Transparent background | An alpha channel, useful for compositing assets                                        | Requires support from the model, parameters, and file format; asking for transparency does not guarantee an alpha channel                                |
| Image count            | Number of generated images or candidates; fields and limits vary by protocol and model | Writing “generate three images” in the prompt is not the same as setting an API count; multiple inputs do not imply multiple outputs                     |

At a fixed aspect ratio, doubling both edges produces four times as many pixels, but does not guarantee a proportional increase in detail or sharpness. Start with the intended use, then check model support, latency, and pricing rather than always choosing the highest tier.

For fields, accepted values, and code examples, see [OpenAI request format](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/openai/generations), [Gemini request format](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/gemini/generate), [Qwen request format](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/qwen/generations), [Jimeng request format](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/jimeng), [Grok request format](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/grok), and [FLUX request format](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/flux). OpenAI's quality, format, and transparency settings are covered in the [official output options](https\://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-generation#customize-image-output); Qwen's dimension and output requirements are in the [official specifications](https\://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/qwen-image-api). Do not copy one protocol's parameters into another.

### How this site's 1K, 2K, and 4K per-image billing tiers differ

The table below applies only to models explicitly priced per image in three 1K / 2K / 4K tiers under [Model pricing](https://api.dwchainless.com/en/pricing/). Token-priced models and models with other fixed prices follow their own rules. An “image model” name alone does not determine how it is billed.

| Billing tier | Longest edge                          | Example dimensions (pixels) |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| 1K           | Both edges ≤ 1024 pixels              | 1024×1024                   |
| 2K           | Longest edge > 1024 and ≤ 2048 pixels | 1280×720, 1536×1024         |
| 4K           | Either edge > 2048 pixels             | 2560×1440, 3840×2160        |

**Total price = per-image price for the current tier × billable image count.** Interfaces supporting settlement by completed results charge for the actual completed count; intermediate streaming previews are not completed images. Current model pricing and usage logs determine the unit price, group, and final charge. This page does not fix numerical prices.

Under these three-tier per-image rules, omitting `size` or using `auto` defaults to 1K only when no other valid resolution tier has been specified. Explicit native resolution fields still determine the billing tier. Pixel dimensions are classified by the longest requested edge, not total pixel count. For example, `1280x720` is 2K and `2560x1440` is 4K.

**A billing tier is not a promise of output dimensions.** Gemini's `generationConfig.imageConfig.imageSize` selects a native model resolution; confirm actual pixel dimensions against the model and aspect ratio. This site calculates billing tiers from supported request fields without promising uniform output dimensions. Do not send conflicting dimension fields, or apply these per-image rules to official direct calls or token-priced models.

### Common ratios at a glance\: 14 ratios × 1K / 2K / 4K

The table lists common 1K, 2K, and 4K preset dimensions by aspect ratio for quickly picking a frame. It is a size quick reference, not a model-support list\: available ratios, preset names, and per-side limits vary by model and gateway, so confirm against the model documentation or API error before requesting.

A K tier here is a preset name, not this page's per-image billing tier. For some "1K" presets the longest edge already exceeds 1024 pixels, which this site classifies as 2K; for example, the 16\:9 1K preset `1536x864` is 2K. Billing always follows the requested dimensions and [Models and pricing](https://api.dwchainless.com/en/pricing/).

| Ratio     | Common use                        | 1K size     | 2K size     | 4K size                 |
| :-------- | :-------------------------------- | :---------- | :---------- | :---------------------- |
| `1:1`     | Square avatar / product           | `1024x1024` | `2048x2048` | `3840x3840`             |
| `4:3`     | Landscape illustration / display  | `1152x896`  | `2048x1536` | `3840x2880`             |
| `3:4`     | Portrait poster / people          | `896x1152`  | `1536x2048` | `2880x3840`             |
| `16:9`    | Landscape cover / slides          | `1536x864`  | `2048x1152` | `3840x2160`             |
| `9:16`    | Vertical cover / phone background | `864x1536`  | `1152x2048` | `2160x3840`             |
| `3:2`     | Landscape photography             | `1536x1024` | `2048x1360` | `3840x2560`             |
| `2:3`     | Portrait photography              | `1024x1536` | `1360x2048` | `2560x3840`             |
| `5:4`     | Landscape product display         | `1280x1024` | `2560x2048` | `3840x3072`             |
| `4:5`     | Portrait product / social image   | `1024x1280` | `2048x2560` | `3072x3840`             |
| `21:9`    | Wide scene / banner               | `1792x768`  | `2048x880`  | `3840x1648`             |
| `1:4`     | Narrow vertical strip             | `512x2048`  | `768x3072`  | **Over per-side limit** |
| `4:1`     | Narrow horizontal strip           | `2048x512`  | `3072x768`  | **Over per-side limit** |
| `1.414:1` | Approx. A-series landscape paper  | `1440x1024` | `2048x1456` | `3840x2720`             |
| `1:1.414` | Approx. A-series portrait paper   | `1024x1440` | `1456x2048` | `2720x3840`             |

### Three correct ways to write size

Some OpenAI-compatible gateways accept the following forms; whether a field takes effect depends on the model and gateway, so fall back to explicit pixels when unsupported.

| Form                          | Request fragment                   | Purpose                                                               |
| :---------------------------- | :--------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Explicit pixels (recommended) | `{"size":"1536x2048"}`             | Most direct; avoids preset conversion differences                     |
| Ratio + resolution            | `{"size":"3:4","resolution":"2k"}` | Converts using the 2K, 3\:4 preset                                    |
| Automatic size                | `{"size":"auto"}`                  | The model chooses dimensions; fixed width and height are not promised |

* Put the K tier in `resolution` and pixels or a ratio in `size`; do not write `2k` in `size`.
* Use a lowercase English `x` as the dimension separator; do not use a multiplication sign, uppercase X, arrays, or strings with ×.
* A ratio in `size` takes precedence over `aspect_ratio` alone; explicit pixels or `auto` take precedence over ratio presets.
* The official arbitrary-size limit for gpt-image-2 is 3840×2160; the 4K `1:4` and `4:1` combinations exceed it and are marked as over the per-side limit. Other models follow their own published limits.
* Gemini and Qwen use their own size fields; these forms do not transfer directly.

### 28 common dimension references

The labels below indicate only the billing tiers defined above; they do not guarantee that the selected model supports these dimensions. Check the model's accepted dimensions first. Do not treat a billing tier as an API parameter value.

| Use / ratio                    | Dimensions (pixels) and billing tier                                         |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| General square · 1\:1          | 1024×1024 · 1K; 1536×1536 · 2K; 2048×2048 · 2K                               |
| Landscape cover · 16\:9        | 1280×720 · 2K; 1536×864 · 2K; 2048×1152 · 2K; 2560×1440 · 4K; 3840×2160 · 4K |
| Vertical video / Story · 9\:16 | 720×1280 · 2K; 864×1536 · 2K; 1152×2048 · 2K; 1440×2560 · 4K; 2160×3840 · 4K |
| Article illustration · 3\:2    | 1536×1024 · 2K; 1920×1280 · 2K; 2400×1600 · 4K                               |
| Portrait poster · 2\:3         | 1024×1536 · 2K; 1280×1920 · 2K; 1600×2400 · 4K                               |
| Wide banner · 2\:1             | 1536×768 · 2K; 2048×1024 · 2K; 2560×1280 · 4K; 3840×1920 · 4K                |
| Ultra-wide banner · 3\:1       | 1536×512 · 2K; 1920×640 · 2K; 2400×800 · 4K; 3072×1024 · 4K; 3840×1280 · 4K  |
