* [OpenAI conversational image generation](https\://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-generation)
* [OpenAI Responses API](https\://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses/methods/create)
* [OpenAI error handling](https\://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/error-codes)

# Image editing and image-to-image

## Endpoint overview

`POST /v1/images/edits` accepts reference images and editing instructions and returns edited images. It can replace backgrounds, transfer styles, add or remove elements, or combine references.

The gateway URL is `https://api.dwchainless.com`, with the request header `Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY`. Direct OpenAI access uses `https://api.openai.com` and Bearer authentication, but requires an OpenAI key. Select a model available to the account that supports the required capability.

Supports JSON images\[] references and multipart uploads. The examples pass a server-accessible HTTPS image URL through JSON `images[].image_url`; they do not use multipart uploads.

## Quick start

1. **Prepare configuration**\: Create a key under [API key management](https://api.dwchainless.com/keys), and copy an editing-capable image model ID from [Models and pricing](https://api.dwchainless.com/en/pricing/).
2. **Prepare reference images**\: Use server-accessible HTTPS image URLs, or upload local files through multipart; do not mix both in one request.
3. **Send the request**\: Send JSON to `https://api.dwchainless.com/v1/images/edits` containing `model`, `prompt`, and image references; use the header `Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY`.
4. **Read and verify**\: Success requires HTTP 2xx and a non-empty `data[]`; decode `data[].b64_json` or download `data[].url`, then check the file, dimensions, and content.

For the first call, edit a single image without streaming; once it works, add more references or enable streaming.

## Request parameters

| Field                | Type    | Required        | Description                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------- | ------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| model                | string  | Yes (gateway)   | Explicitly choose an editing-capable image model rather than relying on upstream defaults.                                                                                      |
| images               | array   | Yes (JSON)      | Image reference list; native GPT Image allows up to 16 images, with potentially stricter model limits.                                                                          |
| images\[].image\_url | string  | Conditional     | An HTTPS image URL or data\:image/...;base64,...; this page’s example uses an HTTPS URL.                                                                                        |
| images\[].file\_id   | string  | Conditional     | An official Files resource ID; use either this or image\_url. Gateway availability must not be assumed.                                                                         |
| prompt               | string  | Yes             | Clearly describe what to change and preserve.                                                                                                                                   |
| mask                 | object  | No              | For JSON, reference mask.image\_url or mask.file\_id; mask rules vary by model.                                                                                                 |
| image / image\[]     | file    | Yes (multipart) | One or more multipart image fields; do not mix with JSON images.                                                                                                                |
| mask (multipart)     | file    | No              | A PNG mask whose transparent regions mark editing areas; match source dimensions and model requirements.                                                                        |
| input\_fidelity      | string  | No              | Only for models supporting this parameter; not every GPT Image generation accepts it.                                                                                           |
| n                    | integer | No              | Image count; native OpenAI GPT Image supports 1–10, with 1 in the example.                                                                                                      |
| size                 | string  | No              | Native OpenAI form is WIDTHxHEIGHT (width and height divisible by 16, aspect ratio 1\:3–3\:1) or auto; SimiRouter also accepts ratio plus resolution, and limits vary by model. |
| resolution           | string  | No              | SimiRouter extension\: tier 1k, 2k, or 4k used with a ratio, not a pixel value; the native OpenAI API has no such field.                                                        |
| aspect\_ratio        | string  | No              | SimiRouter extension\: separate ratio such as 3\:4; a ratio in size takes precedence.                                                                                           |
| quality              | string  | No              | auto, low, medium, or high; some newer models also support xhigh and max.                                                                                                       |
| output\_format       | string  | No              | png, jpeg (examples), or webp; the official schema also lists gif and svg where the model and project access support them.                                                      |
| output\_compression  | integer | No              | JPEG/WebP compression quality from 0–100; not applicable to PNG.                                                                                                                |
| background           | string  | No              | auto, opaque, or transparent; transparency requires a supported model and PNG/WebP.                                                                                             |
| moderation           | string  | No              | auto or supported low; does not guarantee content-policy approval.                                                                                                              |
| response\_format     | string  | No              | Some compatible models accept url or b64\_json; native GPT Image does not use it.                                                                                               |
| stream               | boolean | No              | true uses image SSE events.                                                                                                                                                     |
| partial\_images      | integer | No              | With stream=true, request 0–3 intermediate images; still wait for the final completion event.                                                                                   |

Choose JSON or multipart. Let the client generate the multipart Content-Type boundary. Masks do not guarantee pixel-perfect edits; inspect final images manually.

## Choosing how to send images

Reference images can enter the request in four ways; choose one according to your environment and do not mix them in one request\:

| Form           | Field                         | When to use                                                  |
| -------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| JSON URL       | `images[].image_url`          | The image is public and server-accessible                    |
| JSON Base64    | `images[].image_url` data URL | The image is small and should not be exposed at a public URL |
| multipart file | `image` or `image[]`          | Local files uploaded directly by the client                  |
| Files ID       | `images[].file_id`            | Uploaded through official Files and supported by the gateway |

JSON requests use `Content-Type: application/json`; for multipart, the client must generate the `Content-Type` boundary; do not write it by hand.

### JSON request structure

The JSON example uses a server-accessible HTTPS image URL directly.

```json
{
  "model": "gpt-image-2",
  "images": [
    {
      "image_url": "https://example.com/reference.png"
    }
  ],
  "prompt": "保留主体形状和布局，将图片改成水彩插画，背景改为浅蓝色。",
  "n": 1,
  "size": "1024x1024",
  "output_format": "png"
}
```

### multipart request structure

Use the `image` field for one local reference; use `image[]` for multiple images and describe each image’s role in order\:

```bash
API_URL="https://api.dwchainless.com/v1/images/edits"
API_KEY="PASTE_API_KEY_HERE"
curl "$API_URL" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -F "model=gpt-image-2" \
  -F "prompt=保留主体和构图，将背景改为浅蓝色。" \
  -F "image=@reference.png" \
  -F "size=1024x1024" \
  -F "n=1"
```

## Writing edit prompts

An edit prompt should state both what to preserve and what to change; just writing “make it watercolor” can make the model redraw the whole scene. Organize it as “preserve + change + constraint”\:

| Scenario                     | Prompt focus                                                        | Example                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Preserve a person or product | Keep the subject, pose, composition, and text unchanged             | Keep the person’s pose and clothing; change only the background to pale blue.                          |
| Style transfer               | State the target style and the layout to keep                       | Change to a watercolor illustration style while keeping the original composition and subject position. |
| Local edit                   | Name the region to change; use `mask` when the model supports it    | Change only the cup in the lower-left corner; keep everything else unchanged.                          |
| Multi-image composition      | Describe each image’s role, subject relationships, and final layout | The first image is the person, the second is the scene; place the person in the center of the scene.   |

“Preserve” is a goal, not a pixel-level guarantee; people, products, and text may still change, and identity- or brand-related content must be reviewed manually. Transparency requires model support for `background: transparent` and PNG or WebP output.

## Size and format

`size` sets the model-supported pixel dimensions, such as `1024x1024`; `quality` controls quality and `output_format` controls PNG/JPEG/WebP encoding. The edit result’s dimensions come from `size` (it defaults to `auto`, letting the model choose) and need not match the reference image exactly.

This site’s 1K, 2K, and 4K per-image billing tiers and vendor resolution labels are separate rules; see [Image specifications and billing](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images) for the three ways to write size, the 14-ratio quick reference, and billing boundaries.

## Response

| Field                                                | Type    | Description                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| created                                              | integer | Creation time in Unix seconds.                                                            |
| data\[]                                              | array   | Generated result list; a first item is not guaranteed.                                    |
| data\[].b64\_json                                    | string  | Base64 image bytes; GPT Image uses this format.                                           |
| data\[].url                                          | string  | Present only for compatible models supporting URL output; not a required GPT Image field. |
| data\[].revised\_prompt                              | string  | Revised prompts from some older or compatible models; not required for GPT Image.         |
| output\_format / size / quality / background         | string  | Optional effective output settings.                                                       |
| usage                                                | object  | Optional usage data; availability and granularity vary by model and service.              |
| usage.input\_tokens / output\_tokens / total\_tokens | integer | Input, output, and total tokens, if returned.                                             |
| usage.input\_tokens\_details                         | object  | Optional breakdowns such as image\_tokens and text\_tokens.                               |
| X-Request-Id                                         | string  | Response header, not a JSON field; keep it for support or debugging.                      |

```json
{
  "created": 1760000000,
  "data": [
    {
      "b64_json": "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAQAAAC1HAwCAAAAC0lEQVR42mP8/x8AAwMCAO+j0Z0AAAAASUVORK5CYII="
    }
  ],
  "output_format": "png"
}
```

Example Base64 is a minimal PNG illustrating fields only. A returned data\[].url may expire; do not attach the API key when downloading the image. Streaming edits use image\_edit.partial\_image and image\_edit.completed; only the final event establishes completed editing. Image-to-image does not guarantee pixel-perfect preservation of people, products, or text.

## Code examples

Fill in `API_URL` and `API_KEY` at the top of the code; the examples use `gpt-image-2`. `API_URL` is the full request URL and defaults to the gateway `https://api.dwchainless.com`. `IMAGE_URL` is an HTTPS image URL that the server can access. The examples use standard libraries only, send one request, and print the returned JSON to stdout; they do not save images automatically.

    ```python
    import json
    import urllib.request

    API_URL = "https://api.dwchainless.com/v1/images/edits"

        API_URL,

        headers={

            "Content-Type": "application/json",
    ```

## Errors

| HTTP status     | Meaning or vendor error type                           | Action                                                                                                           |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 400             | Invalid request                                        | Check required fields, JSON, model parameters, and context length.                                               |
| 401             | Authentication failed                                  | Check that the key exists, is valid, and belongs to the correct service.                                         |
| 403 / 404       | Access denied / resource not found                     | Check model permissions, resource IDs, and the URL.                                                              |
| 413             | Request body or image too large                        | Prefer image URLs; reduce Base64 size or image dimensions.                                                       |
| 429             | Rate or quota limit                                    | Distinguish rate limits from insufficient quota using the response body; retrying cannot fix insufficient quota. |
| 500 / 502 / 503 | Server error / busy upstream / temporarily unavailable | Retain the request identifier and use bounded backoff for transient failures.                                    |

Native OpenAI errors usually contain `error.message`, `error.type`, `error.param`, `error.code`; `param`, `code` may be `null`; do not assume these fields always exist or equal the HTTP status. The gateway may return authentication, routing, or quota errors before contacting the vendor; the status alone does not establish an upstream error. Invalid images, MIME mismatches, incompatible mask dimensions, or unsupported parameters are input errors; correct them instead of resubmitting unchanged.

Editing can take tens of seconds to minutes; set a sufficient client timeout, since a hanging request is not a failure. After a timeout, broken stream, or 5xx, first confirm whether the request already executed before retrying, to avoid duplicate generation and charges. When content policy rejects a request (usually 400), revise the prompt or reference image instead of retrying unchanged.

# Image generation

## Endpoint overview

`POST /v1/images/generations` generates one or more images from prompt.

The gateway URL is `https://api.dwchainless.com`, with the request header `Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY`. Direct OpenAI access uses `https://api.openai.com` and Bearer authentication, but requires an OpenAI key. Select a model available to the account that supports the required capability.

This page uses GPT Image parameters. OpenAI-compatible image models from different vendors may accept different sizes, quality levels, and output formats; these differences are not one official standard.

## Quick start

1. **Prepare configuration**\: Create a key under [API key management](https://api.dwchainless.com/keys), and copy an Images API–capable model ID from [Models and pricing](https://api.dwchainless.com/en/pricing/).
2. **Send the request**\: POST JSON to `https://api.dwchainless.com/v1/images/generations` with the header `Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY`; the body must contain at least `model` and `prompt`.
3. **Read the result**\: Success requires HTTP 2xx and a non-empty `data[]`; decode and save GPT Image's `data[].b64_json`.
4. **Confirm completion**\: Check that the file opens and matches the required dimensions, then inspect usage logs.

The minimal request follows; once it works, adjust the count, size, or streaming\:

```bash
API_URL="https://api.dwchainless.com/v1/images/generations"
API_KEY="PASTE_API_KEY_HERE"
curl "$API_URL" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-image-2",
    "prompt": "一只小机器人在图书馆阅读，水彩插画，不要文字。",
    "n": 1,
    "size": "1024x1024",
    "output_format": "png"
  }'
```

## Request parameters

The request body is JSON.

| Field               | Type    | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| model               | string  | Yes      | An image-model ID supporting the Images API.                                                                                                                                    |
| prompt              | string  | Yes      | Describe the subject, composition, style, and text precisely.                                                                                                                   |
| n                   | integer | No       | Image count; native OpenAI GPT Image supports 1–10, with 1 in the example.                                                                                                      |
| size                | string  | No       | Native OpenAI form is WIDTHxHEIGHT (width and height divisible by 16, aspect ratio 1\:3–3\:1) or auto; SimiRouter also accepts ratio plus resolution, and limits vary by model. |
| resolution          | string  | No       | SimiRouter extension\: tier 1k, 2k, or 4k used with a ratio, not a pixel value; the native OpenAI API has no such field.                                                        |
| aspect\_ratio       | string  | No       | SimiRouter extension\: separate ratio such as 3\:4; a ratio in size takes precedence.                                                                                           |
| quality             | string  | No       | auto, low, medium, or high; some newer models also support xhigh and max.                                                                                                       |
| output\_format      | string  | No       | png, jpeg (examples), or webp; the official schema also lists gif and svg where the model and project access support them.                                                      |
| output\_compression | integer | No       | JPEG/WebP compression quality from 0–100; not applicable to PNG.                                                                                                                |
| background          | string  | No       | auto, opaque, or transparent; transparency requires a supported model and PNG/WebP.                                                                                             |
| moderation          | string  | No       | auto or supported low; does not guarantee content-policy approval.                                                                                                              |
| response\_format    | string  | No       | Some compatible models accept url or b64\_json; native GPT Image does not use it.                                                                                               |
| stream              | boolean | No       | true uses image SSE events.                                                                                                                                                     |
| partial\_images     | integer | No       | With stream=true, request 0–3 intermediate images; still wait for the final completion event.                                                                                   |

GPT Image returns Base64 directly; do not rely on the legacy response\_format=url/b64\_json. Some compatible models can use that field to choose a URL or Base64, subject to model documentation and the actual response. The old style=vivid/natural setting also does not apply; describe style in prompt.

### Request example

```json
{
  "model": "gpt-image-2",
  "prompt": "一只小机器人在图书馆阅读，水彩插画，柔和蓝金色调，不要文字。",
  "n": 1,
  "size": "1024x1024",
  "output_format": "png"
}
```

## Image size and format

K is a common resolution label, not file size or a quality setting. Actual dimensions depend on the model and aspect ratio. At the same ratio, doubling both edges quadruples the pixel count. The examples below explain the terms; they are not universally accepted sizes.

OpenAI uses `size` for model-supported dimensions such as `1024x1024`, not the literal `1K`; `quality` and `output_format` independently control quality and format.

| Resolution label | Common pixel examples (not a model support guarantee)       |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1K               | 1024×1024 · About one thousand pixels per edge              |
| 2K               | 2048×2048 · About two thousand pixels per edge              |
| 4K               | 4096×4096 / 3840×2160 · About four thousand pixels per edge |

The site’s per-image billing tiers are separate rules; do not use these illustrative resolution labels as the billing standard. [Image specifications and billing rules](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images).

### Three ways to write size

Some OpenAI-compatible gateways also accept a ratio plus resolution or an automatic size; whether a field takes effect depends on the model and gateway, so fall back to explicit pixels when unsupported.

| Form                          | Request fragment                   | Notes                                                              |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Explicit pixels (recommended) | `{"size":"1536x2048"}`             | Most direct; avoids preset conversion differences.                 |
| Ratio + resolution            | `{"size":"3:4","resolution":"2k"}` | Uses the 2K, 3\:4 preset; resolution accepts only 1k, 2k, 4k.      |
| Automatic size                | `{"size":"auto"}`                  | The model chooses width and height; fixed pixels are not promised. |

* A ratio in size takes precedence over a separate aspect\_ratio; explicit pixels or auto take precedence over ratio presets.
* Put the tier in resolution; do not send size=2k. Use a lowercase English x as the dimension separator.
* For gpt-image-2 the official arbitrary-size limit is 3840×2160; larger combinations such as 4096×4096 generally return a parameter error. The 4K row is a tier illustration, not a guaranteed pixel size.
* For a quick reference of 14 common ratios at 1K, 2K, and 4K, see [Image specifications and billing rules](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images).

| data\[].b64\_json                                    | string  | Base64 image bytes; GPT Image uses this format.                                           |
| data\[].url                                          | string  | Present only for compatible models supporting URL output; not a required GPT Image field. |
| data\[].revised\_prompt                              | string  | Revised prompts from some older or compatible models; not required for GPT Image.         |
| output\_format / size / quality / background         | string  | Optional effective output settings.                                                       |
| usage                                                | object  | Optional usage data; availability and granularity vary by model and service.              |
| usage.input\_tokens / output\_tokens / total\_tokens | integer | Input, output, and total tokens, if returned.                                             |
| usage.input\_tokens\_details                         | object  | Optional breakdowns such as image\_tokens and text\_tokens.                               |

```json

    }
```

### Streaming generation

Supported models accept stream=true, with image\_generation.partial\_image for previews and image\_generation.completed for final images and usage. Partial images are not final results. If a stream ends without completed, do not mark a preview complete. This endpoint returns no universal pollable background-task ID.

    ```python
        "prompt": "一只小机器人在图书馆阅读，水彩插画，不要文字。",
        "size": "1024x1024",
        "n": 1,
    }
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        API_URL,
        data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
        method="POST",
        headers={
            "Authorization": "Bearer " + API_KEY,
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
        },
    )
    print(urllib.request.urlopen(request).read().decode())
    ```
  </Tab>

## Errors

| HTTP status     | Meaning or vendor error type                           | Action                                                                                                           |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 400             | Invalid request                                        | Check required fields, JSON, model parameters, and context length.                                               |
| 401             | Authentication failed                                  | Check that the key exists, is valid, and belongs to the correct service.                                         |
| 403 / 404       | Access denied / resource not found                     | Check model permissions, resource IDs, and the URL.                                                              |
| 413             | Request body or image too large                        | Prefer image URLs; reduce Base64 size or image dimensions.                                                       |
| 429             | Rate or quota limit                                    | Distinguish rate limits from insufficient quota using the response body; retrying cannot fix insufficient quota. |
| 500 / 502 / 503 | Server error / busy upstream / temporarily unavailable | Retain the request identifier and use bounded backoff for transient failures.                                    |

Native OpenAI errors usually contain `error.message`, `error.type`, `error.param`, `error.code`; `param`, `code` may be `null`; do not assume these fields always exist or equal the HTTP status. The gateway may return authentication, routing, or quota errors before contacting the vendor; the status alone does not establish an upstream error. Empty data, missing image data, or intermediate previews alone do not establish completed generation under HTTP 200.

Generation and editing can take tens of seconds to minutes; set a sufficient client timeout, since a hanging request is not the same as a failure. After a timeout, broken stream, or 5xx, first confirm whether the request already executed before retrying, to avoid duplicate generation and charges. When content policy rejects a request (usually 400), revise the prompt or reference image instead of retrying unchanged.

# OpenAI-format image interfaces

This section uses the OpenAI format and distinguishes generation, editing, conversational image generation, and image understanding. Complete one single-image call before increasing the count or connecting an agent. The selected model must support the required image capability.

## Calling order

1. **Prepare configuration**\: Create a key under [API key management](https://api.dwchainless.com/keys), and copy a supported full model ID from [Models and pricing](https://api.dwchainless.com/en/pricing/); the request URL is the gateway `https://api.dwchainless.com`, and the header is `Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY`.
2. **Choose an endpoint**\: use `POST /v1/images/generations` for text-to-image, `POST /v1/images/edits` for editing / image-to-image, `POST /v1/responses` for conversational image generation, and `POST /v1/chat/completions` for image understanding.
3. **Send a minimal request first**\: request a single image without streaming; confirm authentication, model, and parameters are valid before increasing count, size, or connecting an agent.
4. **Read and verify**\: decode Base64 from `data[]` or download the URL, check that the file opens and that dimensions and content meet requirements, then check the usage logs.

Full parameters, examples, and error handling are on the protocol pages below; start with [generation](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/openai/generations) for the first call.

## Request format and parameters

| API                             | Request format                                    | Main parameters                                                                   | Detailed documentation                                            |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Text-to-image                   | `POST /v1/images/generations`, JSON               | `model`, `prompt`; set `n`, `size`, and `quality` according to the model          | [Generation parameters and code in four languages](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/openai/generations) |
| Editing / image-to-image        | `POST /v1/images/edits`, either JSON or multipart | `model`, `prompt`, and `images[]` or the `image` file; add `mask` where supported | [Editing parameters and code in four languages](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/openai/edits)          |
| Conversational image generation | `POST /v1/responses`, JSON                        | `input`, the image generation tool, and its model configuration                   | [Conversational image generation](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/openai/chat-format)                  |
| Image understanding             | `POST /v1/chat/completions`, JSON                 | Text and image content items within `messages`, using `image_url`                 | [Image understanding](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/openai/vision)                                   |

Editing prompts should distinguish what to keep from what to change. Style transfer, background replacement, and adding or removing objects are editing goals, not another API. Masks, multiple input images, and transparent backgrounds require support from the selected model. Pixel-perfect preservation of people, products, or text is not guaranteed.

### Image specifications

`size` expresses pixel dimensions, such as `1024x1024`, rather than a universal `1K` / `2K` / `4K` enumeration; accepted dimensions vary by model. `quality` controls quality and `output_format` controls PNG/JPEG/WebP encoding. Neither replaces resolution. Transparent backgrounds also require model support for `background: transparent` and PNG or WebP output.

The three ways to write size, the 14-ratio quick reference, and the 1K/2K/4K per-image billing tiers are covered in the [image specifications and billing overview](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images). The billing table applies only to models that explicitly use this rule in [Models and pricing](https://api.dwchainless.com/en/pricing/), and does not guarantee that every example dimension is accepted.

## Response parameters

| Response field / event                                | Meaning and handling                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Images `data[].b64_json`                              | GPT Image's Base64 image data; decode and save it as a binary image, rather than renaming the whole JSON to PNG.                 |
| Images `data[].url`                                   | May appear only for older or compatible models with URL output; download promptly and do not assume GPT Image always returns it. |
| Images `usage`                                        | Optional usage data; the presence of this field does not necessarily mean token-based billing.                                   |
| `image_generation.completed` / `image_edit.completed` | Final Images streaming generation / editing events; `partial_image` is only an intermediate preview.                             |
| Responses `output[]`                                  | Handle conversational generation through image-tool output items, not Images `data[]`.                                           |
| Chat `choices[].message.content`                      | Image understanding returns text analysis rather than generated images.                                                          |

## Calling examples

### Prepare configuration

Create a key in [API key management](https://api.dwchainless.com/keys), copy the exact image model ID available to that key from [Models and pricing](https://api.dwchainless.com/en/pricing/), and check permissions, group, and quota. Fill in API\_URL, API\_KEY, and MODEL directly in the example\:

| Variable    | Purpose                                                                                                       |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `API_KEY`   | Required; set directly in the example, never paste into prompts, source files, screenshots, or Git.           |
| `MODEL`     | Required; separately confirm that the model supports the generation or editing endpoint.                      |
| `API_URL`   | Complete request URL; the examples use the gateway `https://api.dwchainless.com`.                             |
| `IMAGE_URL` | An HTTPS image URL used by the editing example; the server must be able to access a PNG, JPEG, or WebP image. |

The [generation examples](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/openai/generations) and [editing examples](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/openai/edits) provide Python, Node.js, curl, and Go. Choose one language and first request only one non-streaming image. The Python 3.8+ and Node.js 20+ examples use standard libraries. Save generation code as `generate.py` or `generate.mjs`, and editing code as `edit.py` or `edit.mjs`; run the relevant file, for example `python3 generate.py` or `node generate.mjs`. Both the Python and Node.js editing examples use JSON `images[].image_url` and do not use multipart uploads.

### Agent editing demo

Confirm permission to process the reference image and check for personal information or trade secrets. Authorize only the necessary files. “Keep” in a prompt expresses a goal, not a pixel-level guarantee.

```text

MODEL, and API_URL directly in the example; use the configured SimiRouter request URL;
never reveal the key or change the existing connection. Use only the authorized HTTPS

or timeout. Ask before another paid request.
```

## Saving and completion criteria

* Before saving, check the HTTP status, final image fields, decoding result, and actual file format. Renaming an extension does not convert the format. On failure, clean up only invalid files created by this attempt; do not delete existing files.
* Start with a single-image, non-streaming request. Streaming requires the corresponding `completed` event; handle multiple results by image index. Without a terminal result, do not mark previews as completed. Standard Images is not a universal asynchronous queue that first returns a task ID for polling.
* Check that the file exists, opens, and meets dimension and content requirements, then check usage logs. HTTP success or an agent saying “done” does not establish that the image was saved.

## Errors, retries, and charges

For 400, check the model and parameters; for 401, check the key; for 403/404, check permissions, model ID, and path; for 429, check quota and rate limits. After a 5xx, timeout, or interrupted stream, inspect logs and existing results before doing anything else. Do not resend automatically, which can duplicate generation or charges. Report only redacted errors and request identifiers, not keys, complete image Base64, or private image content.

Real generation and editing may incur charges. Confirm the model, dimensions, image count, and output location before calling. Increasing `n`, selecting a higher tier, changing models, or retrying requires renewed confirmation. Parallel requests have separate rate limits, timeouts, and charges; `n` is the image count in a single request, not concurrency. Current model pricing and usage logs determine the final charge.

# Image understanding

## Endpoint overview

`POST /v1/chat/completions` combines a text question and images in a user message and returns textual analysis. Image understanding is not generation or editing.

The gateway URL is `https://api.dwchainless.com`, with the request header `Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY`. Direct OpenAI access uses `https://api.openai.com` and Bearer authentication, but requires an OpenAI key. Select a model available to the account that supports the required capability.

Images can use accessible HTTPS URLs or data URLs containing actual media bytes. Examples use an accessible HTTPS image URL.

## Request parameters

| Field                       | Type    | Required    | Description                                                         |
| --------------------------- | ------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| model                       | string  | Yes         | A chat model supporting vision input.                               |
| messages\[].role            | string  | Yes         | Image messages use user.                                            |
| messages\[].content         | array   | Yes         | Include at least a question and an image content item.              |
| content\[].type=text / text | string  | Conditional | The text-question content item.                                     |
| content\[].type=image\_url  | string  | Conditional | Declares an image content item.                                     |
| image\_url.url              | string  | Yes         | An HTTPS URL or data\:image/\{format};base64,...; not a local path. |
| image\_url.detail           | string  | No          | Model-supported detail options such as auto, low, or high.          |
| max\_completion\_tokens     | integer | No          | The output token limit.                                             |
| stream                      | boolean | No          | true returns Chat SSE.                                              |

Use matching MIME types for PNG, JPEG, WebP, and other supported formats. Image count, pixel limits, and request size must meet model requirements. Do not relabel animated GIFs, videos, or arbitrary binary data as image/png.

### Request structure

```json
{
  "model": "gpt-5.5",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": [
        {
          "type": "text",
          "text": "描述图片中的主要物体，并指出无法确定的细节。"
        },
        {
          "type": "image_url",
          "image_url": {
            "url": "data:image/png;base64,BASE64_IMAGE_BYTES",
            "detail": "auto"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "max_completion_tokens": 512,
  "stream": false
}
```

## Response

| Field                          | Type             | Description                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| id / object                    | string           | Response ID; object=chat.completion.                                                                                                                |
| created / model                | integer / string | Creation time in Unix seconds and the responding model.                                                                                             |
| choices\[]                     | array            | Candidate replies; each index identifies its position.                                                                                              |
| choices\[].message.role        | string           | assistant.                                                                                                                                          |
| choices\[].message.content     | string / null    | Reply text; may be empty for tool calls or refusals, which does not itself mean the request failed.                                                 |
| choices\[].message.tool\_calls | array            | Function calls for the application to execute. arguments is a JSON string that must be parsed and validated.                                        |
| choices\[].message.refusal     | string / null    | Refusal information, if present.                                                                                                                    |
| choices\[].finish\_reason      | string           | stop means normal completion; length means the limit was reached; tool\_calls requests tool execution; content\_filter indicates content filtering. |
| usage.prompt\_tokens           | integer          | Input tokens.                                                                                                                                       |
| usage.completion\_tokens       | integer          | Generated tokens, possibly including reasoning tokens.                                                                                              |
| usage.total\_tokens            | integer          | Total input and generated tokens.                                                                                                                   |
| usage.\*\_tokens\_details      | object           | Optional usage details such as cached\_tokens and reasoning\_tokens.                                                                                |

```json
{
  "id": "chatcmpl_vision_example",
  "object": "chat.completion",
  "choices": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "message": {
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": "图中可见一张桌子和一个杯子，杯内物品无法确认。"
      },
      "finish_reason": "stop"
    }
  ],
  "usage": {
    "prompt_tokens": 280,
    "completion_tokens": 30,
    "total_tokens": 310
  }
}
```

Add image\_url items for multiple images. Specify their order and comparison goals in text. Merge Chat delta.content when streaming. Do not rely solely on vision output for small text, exact counts, identity, or high-risk judgments.

## Code examples

Fill in `API_URL` and `API_KEY` at the top of the code; the examples use `gpt-5.5`. `API_URL` is the full request URL and defaults to the gateway `https://api.dwchainless.com`. `IMAGE_URL` is an HTTPS image URL that the server can access. The examples use standard libraries only, send one request, and print the returned JSON to stdout; they do not save images automatically.

# Qwen image editing

## Endpoint overview

`POST /v1/images/edits`, with a JSON body. The examples use this site's gateway `https://api.dwchainless.com` and a key from this site for `API_KEY`; the request body follows Qwen's native `model`, `input.messages`, and `parameters` structure, and the response is always `data[]`.

Image editing places an image item and one text modification instruction in content; do not use the multipart file field.

## Request parameters

| Field                              | Type      | Required | Description                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------- | --------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| model                              | string    | Yes      | qwen-image-2.0-pro or a specific version supported by this site's channel.                                         |
| input.messages                     | object\[] | Yes      | A single-round user message, exactly one.                                                                          |
| input.messages\[].role             | string    | Yes      | Always user.                                                                                                       |
| input.messages\[].content\[].text  | string    | Yes      | Chinese or English instructions; only one text item per turn.                                                      |
| input.messages\[].content\[].image | string    | Yes      | Accessible URL / data URL for one or more reference images. Input count and pixel limits follow the model version. |
| parameters.size                    | string    | No       | Width × height, such as 2048 × 2048; the 2.0 series supports total pixels from 512×512 to 2048×2048.               |
| parameters.n                       | integer   | No       | Default 1; the 2.0 series supports 1–6.                                                                            |
| parameters.negative\_prompt        | string    | No       | Content you do not want, up to 500 characters.                                                                     |
| parameters.prompt\_extend          | boolean   | No       | Default true; automatically expands the positive prompt.                                                           |
| parameters.watermark               | boolean   | No       | Whether to add a visible watermark; follow applicable synthetic-content labeling requirements.                     |

### Image specifications\: 1K, 2K and 4K

K is a common shorthand for resolution; it is not file size and does not indicate a quality parameter. Actual width and height vary by model and aspect ratio; at the same ratio, doubling the edge length quadruples total pixels. The following is background only and must not be treated directly as the available sizes for every model.

Qwen uses `parameters.size` to enter the width and height allowed by the model, in a format such as `2048*2048`, not `2K` directly. The 2.0 series also has a total-pixel limit; the 4K square illustration below does not mean that size can be submitted.

| Resolution label | Common pixel illustration (not a model support guarantee) |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1K               | Both edges ≤ 1024 pixels; e.g. 1024×1024.                 |
| 2K               | Longest edge > 1024 and ≤ 2048 pixels; e.g. 1280×720.     |
| 4K               | Either edge > 2048 pixels; e.g. 2560×1440.                |

This site's per-image billing tiers are a separate rule; do not apply the illustrative labels above directly as billing standards. [Image specifications and billing rules](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images).

## Response

| Field                   | Description                                                                               |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `created`               | Response generation timestamp.                                                            |
| `data[].url`            | Generated image URL; validity is determined by the channel, so download or copy promptly. |
| `data[].b64_json`       | Some channels return raw Base64; when present, decode and save directly.                  |

## Code examples

Fill in `API_URL` and `API_KEY` at the top of the code. `API_URL` uses this site's gateway address `https://api.dwchainless.com/v1/images/edits`, and `API_KEY` uses a key from this site. The examples use standard libraries only, send one request, and print the returned JSON; they do not download or save images automatically.

Set `IMAGE_URL` to a real, authorized, cloud-accessible HTTP(S) image address. The code checks URL form only and does not prove the image is downloadable or meets the channel's format limits; do not use local paths, localhost, login-protected pages, or fake links.

<Tabs items={["Python","Node.js","curl","Go"]}>
  <Tab value="Python">
    ```python
    import json
    import urllib.request

    API_URL = "https://api.dwchainless.com/v1/images/edits"
    API_KEY = "PASTE_API_KEY_HERE"
    body = {
      "model": "qwen-image-2.0-pro",
      "input": {
        "messages": [
          {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
              {
                "image": "https://example.com/reference.png"
              },
              {
                "text": "保留主体和构图，将背景改为浅蓝色。"
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      },
      "parameters": {
        "size": "1024*1024",
        "n": 1
      }

        method="POST",
        headers={
    ```

# Qwen image generation

## Endpoint overview

`POST /v1/images/generations`, with a JSON body. The examples use this site's gateway `https://api.dwchainless.com` and a key from this site for `API_KEY`; the request body follows Qwen's native `model`, `input.messages`, and `parameters` structure, and the response is always `data[]`.

Text-to-image needs only text content items. Describe composition, visual style, and text to render in the input text.

## Request parameters

| Field                             | Type      | Required | Description                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------- | --------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| model                             | string    | Yes      | qwen-image-2.0-pro or a specific version supported by this site's channel.                           |
| input.messages                    | object\[] | Yes      | A single-round user message, exactly one.                                                            |
| input.messages\[].role            | string    | Yes      | Always user.                                                                                         |
| input.messages\[].content\[].text | string    | Yes      | Chinese or English instructions; only one text item per turn.                                        |
| parameters.size                   | string    | No       | Width × height, such as 2048 × 2048; the 2.0 series supports total pixels from 512×512 to 2048×2048. |
| parameters.n                      | integer   | No       | Default 1; the 2.0 series supports 1–6.                                                              |
| parameters.negative\_prompt       | string    | No       | Content you do not want, up to 500 characters.                                                       |
| parameters.prompt\_extend         | boolean   | No       | Default true; automatically expands the positive prompt.                                             |
| parameters.watermark              | boolean   | No       | Whether to add a visible watermark; follow applicable synthetic-content labeling requirements.       |

### Image specifications\: 1K, 2K and 4K

K is a common shorthand for resolution; it is not file size and does not indicate a quality parameter. Actual width and height vary by model and aspect ratio; at the same ratio, doubling the edge length quadruples total pixels. The following is background only and must not be treated directly as the available sizes for every model.

Qwen uses `parameters.size` to enter the width and height allowed by the model, in a format such as `2048*2048`, not `2K` directly. The 2.0 series also has a total-pixel limit; the 4K square illustration below does not mean that size can be submitted.

| Resolution label | Common pixel illustration (not a model support guarantee) |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1K               | Both edges ≤ 1024 pixels; e.g. 1024×1024.                 |
| 2K               | Longest edge > 1024 and ≤ 2048 pixels; e.g. 1280×720.     |
| 4K               | Either edge > 2048 pixels; e.g. 2560×1440.                |

This site's per-image billing tiers are a separate rule; do not apply the illustrative labels above directly as billing standards. [Image specifications and billing rules](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images).

## Response

| Field                   | Description                                                                               |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `created`               | Response generation timestamp.                                                            |
| `data[].url`            | Generated image URL; validity is determined by the channel, so download or copy promptly. |
| `data[].b64_json`       | Some channels return raw Base64; when present, decode and save directly.                  |
| `data[].revised_prompt` | Prompt rewritten by the channel; may be absent.                                           |
| `error` / `message`     | Error code and description on failure.                                                    |

```json
{"created":1760000000,"data":[{"url":"https://example.com/generated.png","b64_json":null,"revised_prompt":"..."}]}
```

# Qwen native image interfaces

This section uses the native Qwen request body but always calls through this site's gateway\: `API_URL` is `https://api.dwchainless.com/v1/images/...`, and authentication uses this site's `API_KEY`. Request parameters follow `model`, `input.messages`, and `parameters`, and the response is always `data[]`; complete one single-image call first, then increase the count or connect an agent.

## Request format and parameters

| API                      | Request format                      | Main parameters                                                     | Detailed documentation                                            |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Text-to-image            | `POST /v1/images/generations`, JSON | `model`, `input.messages[].content[].text`, `parameters`            | [Generation parameters and code in four languages](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/qwen/generations) |
| Editing / image-to-image | `POST /v1/images/edits`, JSON       | `content[]` containing an `image` and one `text`, plus `parameters` | [Editing parameters and code in four languages](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/qwen/edits)          |

In the 2.0-series examples on this page, `input.messages` contains one `user` message whose text describes the subject, composition, style, and text to render; for editing, add an authorized image URL or a model-supported data URL. Background replacement, style transfer, editing text within images, and multi-image fusion are editing goals; there are no separate OpenAI multipart fields, and pixel-perfect detail preservation is not guaranteed.

### Image specifications

Dimensions go in `parameters.size` in the format `width*height`, for example `"2048*2048"`, not `"2048x2048"` or `"2K"`. The 2.0 series constrains dimensions by total pixel range; check the input image, width, height, and output limits against the model. A total-pixel limit is not a longest-edge limit.

| This site's three-tier per-image billing | Longest requested edge   | Pixel example |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------- |
| 1K                                       | ≤ 1024 pixels            | 1024×1024     |
| 2K                                       | > 1024 and ≤ 2048 pixels | 1536×1024     |
| 4K                                       | > 2048 pixels            | 2560×1440     |

This table explains only the billing tiers of specific models on this site; it does not mean the models accept `1K` / `2K` / `4K` parameters. Calls through this site are billed under [Models and pricing](https://api.dwchainless.com/en/pricing/), and see the [image specifications and billing overview](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images). Larger pixel counts do not guarantee correct text or details; unsupported target specifications should return an error instead of being silently substituted.

## Response parameters

| Response field          | Meaning and handling                                                                          |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `created`               | Response generation timestamp.                                                                |
| `data[].url`            | Final image URL; validity is determined by the channel, so download and save promptly.        |
| `data[].b64_json`       | Some channels return raw Base64; when present, decode and save directly.                      |
| `data[].revised_prompt` | Prompt rewritten by the channel; may be absent.                                               |
| `error` / `message`     | Error code and description; check business errors and image presence even when HTTP succeeds. |

The request body is the native Qwen structure, and the response is the uniform `data[]`. Do not copy another channel's `prompt`, multipart, or asynchronous `task_id` protocol; the model ID must match the actual name provided by this site's channel.

## Calling examples

### Prepare configuration

Check available models and balance under [Models and pricing](https://api.dwchainless.com/en/pricing/), and use a Key created on this site. `API_URL` always points to this site's gateway; no workspace ID, regional domain, or official Model Studio Key is needed.

| Configuration | Purpose                                                                                                                         |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `API_KEY`     | This site's Key; fill it directly in the example, and do not paste it into prompts, code, screenshots, or Git.                  |
| `API_URL`     | Full request address of this site's gateway, such as `https://api.dwchainless.com/v1/images/generations`.                       |
| `model`       | The existing example uses `qwen-image-2.0-pro`; first confirm this site's channel supports the model and required capabilities. |
| `IMAGE_URL`   | Authorized, cloud-accessible HTTP(S) image address used by the editing example; not a local path or localhost.                  |

The [generation examples](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/qwen/generations) and [editing examples](/simidoc/en/apps/api/images/qwen/edits) provide Python, Node.js, curl, and Go. The existing code sends one request and prints JSON; it **does not download images automatically**. Save Python code as `generate.py` / `edit.py` and run `python3 generate.py` / `python3 edit.py`; save Node.js code as `generate.mjs` / `edit.mjs` and run `node generate.mjs` / `node edit.mjs`. Configure the runtime and variables as described on the corresponding page, request only one image first, then save the actual image referenced by the URL as described in the next section.

## Saving and completion criteria

* A synchronous response is not a polling task; this section does not use `task_id` or `X-DashScope-Async`. Do not mix in another model's asynchronous protocol, and do not treat streaming events as completion criteria.
* Check HTTP and business errors, the finish reason, and the actual image items, then traverse the image URLs. URLs have limited validity, so download promptly; JSON, an address, or an agent's verbal conclusion does not mean the file has been saved.
* When downloading, check the response status, content, and file signature; do not rename an error page to PNG. Do not send this site's Key to the result storage domain. Keep the original files, and on failure clean up only the invalid output created by this attempt.
* Confirm that the file exists, opens, and meets the dimension and content requirements, and verify the request and charge in this site's billing or usage logs. Check multiple images one by one; do not call again automatically just to make up the count.

## Errors, retries, and charges

For parameter errors, check `model`, the message structure, `size`, and the input image. For authentication errors, check this site's Key and model permissions. For quota or rate-limit errors, check the account status. After a timeout, 5xx, or unclear result, inspect the call logs and existing files first; do not resend automatically, which can duplicate generation or charges. Report only redacted errors; do not output keys, full Base64, or private images.

Real generation and editing may incur charges. Before calling, confirm the model, dimensions, image count, and output location; incremental changes, specification upgrades, or retries require renewed confirmation. Control rate limits, timeouts, and charges separately for parallel requests; `n` is the count per request. Final pricing is determined by this site's rules and billing.

# Gemini embeddings

**SimiRouter does not currently support this endpoint. The following references direct official Google access.** The examples use a Gemini API key from Google AI Studio. Follow the Google Cloud documentation for Vertex AI request paths, project setup, and authentication.

## Endpoint overview

`POST https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-embedding-2:embedContent` and `x-goog-api-key: $GEMINI_API_KEY`. Examples use text input. Gemini Embedding 2 also supports model-permitted multimodal content, but those capabilities do not apply to older text-embedding models.

## Request parameters

| Field                                   | Type      | Required | Description                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------- | --------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| model (path)                            | string    | Yes      | models/gemini-embedding-2; must be an available embedding model.                        |
| content                                 | object    | Yes      | The Content object to embed, with text in parts\[].text.                                |
| content.parts                           | object\[] | Yes      | Text items, or model-supported inline\_data / file\_data multimodal items.              |
| embedContentConfig                      | object    | No       | Embedding configuration; supported settings follow the model version and API Reference. |
| embedContentConfig.outputDimensionality | integer   | No       | Model-supported output dimensions; keep indexing and queries consistent.                |

`gemini-embedding-2` does not support `embedContentConfig.taskType` or `title`. Use input prefixes for retrieval tasks instead\:

* Query\: `task: search result | query: {content}`
* Document\: `title: {title} | text: {content}`; use `title: none` when there is no title
* Symmetric task\: `task: {task} | query: {content}`

`taskType` and `title` apply only to `gemini-embedding-001`. `gemini-embedding-2` does not support these fields; use the input prefixes above instead of relying on undefined field handling. The vector spaces of embedding-2 and embedding-001 are incompatible, so the index and query sides must use the same model.

The top-level fields `taskType`, `title`, `outputDimensionality` are legacy configuration entries; SDKs use a config object, so do not mix SDK snake\_case with HTTP JSON camelCase.

## Response

A synchronous request returns `embedding.values` as a floating-point array. `batchEmbedContents` accepts a requests array and returns `embeddings[]` in input order. Asynchronous `asyncBatchEmbedContent` returns a long-running task resource requiring separate status and output-file management, unlike this page’s synchronous request.

```json
{"embedding":{"values":[0.01,-0.02,0.03]}}
```

Vectors are excerpted examples. If dimensions are reduced, normalize according to model guidance; the first three elements are not a complete vector.

# Embeddings (unsupported)

**SimiRouter does not currently support embedding endpoints.** This section explains vendor protocols. Examples require direct access with the respective vendor account and key.

## Overview

Embeddings map text or other model-allowed inputs into fixed-length vectors for semantic retrieval, clustering, and similarity analysis. They do not return chat answers or directly execute searches; a retrieval pipeline usually has three stages\: embedding recall of candidates, reranking for precision, and model generation of the answer. See [OpenAI embeddings](/simidoc/en/apps/api/pending/embeddings/openai) and [Gemini embeddings](/simidoc/en/apps/api/pending/embeddings/gemini) for endpoint details.

| What you want to do                         | Input                                     | Output                               | Endpoint                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Generate text vectors                       | One or more text strings                  | Fixed-length float array             | OpenAI `POST /v1/embeddings`; Google `POST /v1beta/models/{model}:embedContent` |
| Generate vectors for images and other media | Multimodal content supported by the model | Float array in the same vector space | Only multimodal models such as `gemini-embedding-2`                             |
| Build an index in batch                     | Multiple text strings                     | Vector list aligned with input order | `batchEmbedContents` or the Batch API; asynchronous batch jobs are separate     |

## Core concepts

* **Dimensions**\: OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` defaults to 1536 dimensions and `text-embedding-3-large` to 3072; Gemini Embedding 2 supports 128–3072 dimensions (recommended 768, 1536, or 3072), while `gemini-embedding-001` defaults to 3072. Dimensions can be lowered within the model range but not raised above its limit; both vendors tie vector-store storage and retrieval cost directly to dimensions.
* **Normalization and similarity**\: OpenAI returns unit-length vectors, so the dot product is cosine similarity; Gemini requires renormalization at dimensions other than 3072 (`gemini-embedding-2` handles it automatically, while `gemini-embedding-001` requires manual work). A vector store must fix one distance metric.
* **Index and query must be homogeneous**\: the same document set and queries must use the same model, dimensions, and task configuration. After changing the model or dimensions, the old index and new vectors are not comparable and must be rebuilt.
* **`index` is not a ranking**\: the `index` in the response only identifies which input the vector corresponds to, for alignment with the source text; relevance ranking is the job of reranking, see [Reranking](/simidoc/en/apps/api/pending/rerank).
* **Synchronous and batch**\: embeddings are synchronous requests with no SSE; large batches go through the Batch API or `batchEmbedContents`, not a forced loop of single calls.

## Simulated call

Illustrative request and response for direct OpenAI access. Use the project key `$OPENAI_API_KEY` when sending the request.

```json
{
  "model": "text-embedding-3-small",
  "input": ["文档检索的第一段文本", "如何计算两段文本的相似度"]
}
```

```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    { "object": "embedding", "index": 0, "embedding": [0.0023, -0.0119, 0.0044] },
    { "object": "embedding", "index": 1, "embedding": [0.0011, 0.0087, -0.0026] }
  ],
  "model": "text-embedding-3-small",
  "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 12, "total_tokens": 12 }
}
```

The actual vector has 1536 floats; only the first three are shown here. `usage` bills by input tokens, independent of output length.

## Retrieval essentials

These two response structures are not the same; changing only the model name is not enough. Neither usually offers SSE or Realtime, and asynchronous batch jobs are not live vector streams. Documents and queries in one vector store should use the same model, dimensions, and normalization strategy; changing models usually requires rebuilding the index.

## Official references

* [OpenAI Embeddings](https\://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/embeddings)
* [OpenAI Create embeddings](https\://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/embeddings)
* [Google Embeddings](https\://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/embeddings)

# OpenAI embeddings

**SimiRouter does not currently support this endpoint. The following references direct official OpenAI access.**

## Endpoint overview

`POST https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings`, `Content-Type: application/json`, `Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY`. Each request returns complete vectors; SSE is not supported.

## Request parameters

| Field            | Type                              | Required | Description                                                                                                    |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| model            | string                            | Yes      | An available embedding model such as text-embedding-3-small or text-embedding-3-large.                         |
| input            | string / string\[] / token arrays | Yes      | Nonempty text or token input; up to 2,048 array items, 8,192 tokens per input, and 300,000 tokens per request. |
| dimensions       | integer                           | No       | A positive integer; text-embedding-3 and later supported models can reduce dimensions.                         |
| encoding\_format | string                            | No       | float (default) returns floating-point arrays; base64 returns encoded strings.                                 |
| user             | string                            | No       | An end-user identifier without plaintext personal information.                                                 |

## Response

| Field                                        | Description                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `object`                                     | list.                                                           |
| `data[].object`                              | embedding.                                                      |
| `data[].index`                               | The corresponding input-array position.                         |
| `data[].embedding`                           | A vector array or Base64 string, according to encoding\_format. |
| `model`                                      | The model used.                                                 |
| `usage.prompt_tokens` / `usage.total_tokens` | Token statistics.                                               |

The following omits middle vector elements to illustrate structure only\:

```json
{"object":"list","data":[{"object":"embedding","index":0,"embedding":[0.01,-0.02]}],"model":"text-embedding-3-small","usage":{"prompt_tokens":3,"total_tokens":3}}
```
